Build an ECS · part 2, components · 2.7

Inspecting the world

ecs/src/2.components/2.7.inspecting/inspecting.rin

The world can store, copy and move any component, but it can't show you one. When something goes wrong at frame 3,000, you want to see an entity: every component it has, every field, with names. In C that means writing a printer per component and keeping each in step with its struct. In rin, the compiler already wrote down everything a printer needs. Each component's reflect record lists its fields with their names, types and byte offsets. The world registered those records back in 2.1 to learn component sizes. Here they pay off a second time.

kayan_inspect(w, e)       every component of e, field by field
kayan_print_layout(w)     every table, its columns, and their memory

Neither names a single component type. Add a component tomorrow and both print it.

Step 1: a component as bytes

Tools work from reflect records, not types, so they need the byte view:

kayan_get_bytes: proc(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity, id: u32) -> []u8 = {
    none: []u8 = {};
    if (!kayan_alive(w, e) || id >= w[0].component_count) {
        return none;
    }
    slot: *kayan_slot = vec<kayan_slot>at(w[0].slots&, cast(e.index, u64));
    t: *kayan_table = kayan_table_at(w, slot[0].table);
    if (!kayan_table_has(t, id)) {
        return none;
    }
    c: *kayan_column = t[0].columns[id]&;
    row: u64 = cast(slot[0].row, u64);
    all: []u8 = c[0].data[0..t[0].count * c[0].size];
    return all[row * c[0].size..(row + 1) * c[0].size];
}

It's kayan_get<T>'s path, stopping one step early: the row's bytes as a slice, sized by the column. Game code uses the typed layer; tools use this.

Step 2: walking fields

kayan_print_fields: proc(type: *const reflect, base: []const u8, depth: u32) -> void = {
    fields: [*]const reflect_field = reflect_fields(type);
    for (i: u64 = 0; i < type[0].count; i += 1) {
        f: *const reflect_field = fields[i]&;
        if (reflect_field_has_attr(f, "hidden")) {
            continue;
        }
        at: []const u8 = base[f[0].offset..f[0].offset + f[0].size];
        kayan_indent(depth);
        printf("%s:", f[0].name);
        info: *const reflect = f[0].info;
        if (info != null && info[0].kind == reflect_kind_struct) {
            printf("\n");
            kayan_print_fields(info, at, depth + 1);
        } else {
            printf(" ");
            kayan_print_builtin(f[0].type, at);
            printf("\n");
        }
    }
}

For each field the record says, cut its bytes out of the component by offset and size. A struct field (at: vec2 inside position) has a record of its own, so the printer recurses into it. A builtin field (f32, u32) is printed by its type's name.

Because each field's bytes are cut with a bounds-checked slice, a record that disagreed with the data would stop a Debug build instead of printing garbage.

Step 3: hiding bookkeeping

Fields can carry tags with @:

turret: struct = { cooldown: f32; timer: f32 @ "hidden"; }

The inspector skips anything tagged "hidden". The component decides what a tool shows; the tool doesn't need to know the component.

Step 4: an entity, and the layout

kayan_inspect walks the entity's signature and prints each component with kayan_print_fields. kayan_print_layout walks every table and prints each column's row size and bytes used out of bytes allocated, which shows where memory goes.

Run it

0:1 {position turret}
    position
        at:
            x: 0.00
            y: 0.00
    turret
        cooldown: 0.50
...
2:1 {position velocity health burning}
...
    health
        points: 60.00
        max: 100.00
    burning
        per_second: 10.00
...
1:1 (dead)
table 1 {position velocity health}: 0 rows, room for 4
    position   8 bytes a row,    0 of   32 bytes in use
    velocity   8 bytes a row,    0 of   32 bytes in use
    health     8 bytes a row,    0 of   32 bytes in use

The turret's timer isn't printed. Table 1 is empty but keeps its capacity: drone 1:1 was its only remaining row after 2:1 caught fire and moved out, and then 1:1 was despawned. Tables never shrink in this course. A real engine might trim empty ones between levels.

Part 2 in one picture

handle 2:1 ──> slots[2] { generation 1, table 2, row 0 }
                                         │
table 2 {position velocity health burning}
  entities  [ 2:1 ]
  position  [ (30, -5) ]     velocity [ (-1, 0) ]     health [ 60/100 ]     burning [ 10 ]
  add_edges / remove_edges ──> neighbouring tables in the archetype graph

The storage half of the ECS is done: identity (Part 1), and any component, in any combination, changing at run time (Part 2). Part 3 is the behaviour: queries to find tables, and systems to run over them.

Try

  1. Add a field to health and run it. Nothing in the inspector changes.
  2. Tag health.max as hidden.
  3. Write kayan_set_f32_by_name(w, e, "health", "points", 10.0) with the reflect records: find the component by name, the field by name, check it's an f32, write it. That's the core of an editor or a console.

The pointer is434// good until the next structural change, so use it now and keep the handle.435kayan_get: proc<T>(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity) -> *T = {436    if (!kayan_alive(w, e)) {437        return null;438    }439    slot: *kayan_slot = vec<kayan_slot>at(w[0].slots&, cast(e.index, u64));440    t: *kayan_table = kayan_table_at(w, slot[0].table);441    if (!kayan_table_has(t, kayan_id_of<T>())) {442        return null;443    }444    rows: []T = kayan_slice<T>(t);445    return rows[cast(slot[0].row, u64)]&;446}447 448kayan_has: proc<T>(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity) -> b32 = {449    return (kayan_signature(w, e) & kayan_mask_of<T>()) != 0;450}451 452// Write e's T. It must already have one: giving an entity a component it does453// not have changes its table, which is 2.6.454kayan_set: proc<T>(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity, value: T) -> kayan_status = {455    if (!kayan_alive(w, e)) {456        return kayan_status.dead;457    }458    p: *T = kayan_get<T>(w, e);459    if (p == null) {460        return kayan_status.missing;461    }462    p[0] = value;463    return kayan_status.ok;464}465 466// Give e a T. Build an ECS · part 3, systems · 3.1

Queries

ecs/src/3.systems/3.1.queries/queries.rin

Part 2 finished the storage. Everything from here on is behaviour, and in an ECS behaviour lives in systems: code that runs over every entity with some set of components. "Every entity with a position and a velocity" isn't in one place. It's spread over every table whose signature has both bits. So a system's first job is finding those tables, and the thing that finds them is a query:

all {position velocity}, none {}   ->   tables 1, 2, 3

A query matches tables, not entities. A game has a handful of tables and rarely makes new ones, so the matching is done once and kept. Each frame, a system walks the kept list, and inside each table streams the columns.

Step 1: the query

kayan_query: struct = {
    all: u64;
    none: u64;
    tables: vec<u32>;
    checked: u64;
}
  • all: a table must have every one of these components.
  • none: and none of these. "Drones that aren't burning" is all {health}, none {burning}.
  • tables: the matching tables, by index. Indices, as always, because pointers to tables go stale.
  • checked: how many of the world's tables the query has looked at.

Matching is two ANDs on the signature:

kayan_matches: proc(signature: u64, all: u64, none: u64) -> b32 = {
    return (signature & all) == all && (signature & none) == 0;
}

Step 2: keeping it up to date

Tables are only ever added, always at the end of w.tables, and never removed. So a query that has checked the first checked tables only needs to look at the ones after that:

kayan_query_update: proc(w: *kayan_world, q: *kayan_query) -> void = {
    for (ti: u64 = q[0].checked; ti < w[0].tables.length; ti += 1) {
        if (kayan_matches(kayan_table_at(w, cast(ti, u32))[0].signature, q[0].all, q[0].none)) {
            _ = vec<u32>append(w[0].arena, q[0].tables&, cast(ti, u32));
        }
    }
    q[0].checked = w[0].tables.length;
}

The first update checks every table. After that, a frame with no new tables costs one comparison. A new table is checked once, by each query, the next time each is updated. flecs does the same thing in reverse: when a table is made, it tells the queries.

Step 3: walking a query

This is the shape of every system:

    kayan_query_update(w&, movers&);
    for (i: u64 = 0; i < movers.tables.length; i += 1) {
        t: *kayan_table = kayan_query_table(w&, movers&, i);
        ps: []position = kayan_slice<position>(t);
        vs: []velocity = kayan_slice<velocity>(t);
        for (row: u64 = 0; row < t[0].count; row += 1) {
            ps[row].at.x += vs[row].per_second.x * 0.5;
            ps[row].at.y += vs[row].per_second.y * 0.5;
        }
    }

Two loops. The outer one is over tables, a few iterations. The inner one is over rows: two dense arrays, read and written in order. That's lesson 1's move_soa. The query's job is to hand you the arrays; what you do with them is the same data-oriented loop as always.

The drones and the bullet are in different tables, and the loop doesn't care. The turret isn't matched (no velocity), and the loop never sees it, not even to skip it.

Run it

movers: all {position velocity}, none {}; tables: 2, entities: 4
    table 1 {position velocity health}: 1:1 2:1 3:1
    table 2 {position velocity damage lifetime}: 4:1
targets: all {position health}, none {burning}; tables: 1, entities: 3
    table 1 {position velocity health}: 1:1 2:1 3:1
on_fire: all {health burning}, none {}; tables: 0, entities: 0

Then drone 2:1 catches fire, which makes table 3, after the queries were made:

2:1 catches fire, and the world makes table 3 for it
the queries have checked 3 tables; updating them checks the new one only
movers: all {position velocity}, none {}; tables: 3, entities: 4
    table 1 {position velocity health}: 1:1 3:1
    table 2 {position velocity damage lifetime}: 4:1
    table 3 {position velocity health burning}: 2:1
targets: all {position health}, none {burning}; tables: 1, entities: 2
    table 1 {position velocity health}: 1:1 3:1
on_fire: all {health burning}, none {}; tables: 1, entities: 1
    table 3 {position velocity health burning}: 2:1

movers picked up the new table, targets refused it (none {burning}), and on_fire got its first. Nobody re-scanned the old tables.

Last, the bullet is despawned. Its table is now empty, and stays in movers. Walking an empty table costs one look at count.

Why this is fast

A query's cost doesn't depend on how many entities there are. It depends on how many tables match, and that number is small and stable. 10,000 drones in one table is one table to visit. That's the payoff of grouping entities by signature back in 2.4: the "which entities have X and Y?" question gets answered per table, once, instead of per entity, every frame.

The flip side is archetype fragmentation (2.4's Try): if every entity had a unique signature, every query would match thousands of one-row tables.

Try

  1. Write a query for "everything with a position that isn't a turret" and print it.
  2. Make 100 drones and walk movers. How many times does the outer loop run?
  3. Add any: u64 to the query: at least one of these components. Where in kayan_matches does it go?

Each is131// the table's index plus one, so 0, which a new table starts with, means "not132// known yet".133kayan_table: struct = {134    signature: u64;135    count: u64;136    capacity: u64;137    entities: [*]kayan_entity;138    columns: [64]kayan_column;139    add_edges: [64]u32;140    remove_edges: [64]u32;141}142 143// The world: the registry, the slots and free list, and every table, with a144// map from signature to table index so finding one is a lookup, not a search.145// Tables are referred to by index, never by pointer: making a table can grow146// `tables` and move all of them, and an index survives that.147kayan_world: struct = {148    arena: *memops_arena;149    infos: [64]*const reflect;150    component_count: u32;151    tables: vec<kayan_table>;152    by_signature: hashmap<u64, u32>;153    slots: vec<kayan_slot>;154    free: vec<u32>;155    live: u64;156}157 158kayan_bit: proc(id: u32) -> u64 = {159    return 1'u64 shl cast(id, u64);160}161 162kayan_id_of: proc<T>() -> u32 = {163    return cast(component_of<T>(), u32);164}165 166kayan_mask_of: proc<T>() -> u64 = {167    return kayan_bit(kayan_id_of<T>());168}169 170kayan_register: proc(w: *kayan_world, id: u32, info: *const reflect) -> void = {171    if (id >= 64) {172        printfmt("kayan: component id {} is past the 64 a signature can hold\n", id);173        exit(1);174    }175    w[0].infos[id] = info;176    if (id + 1 > w[0].component_count) {177        w[0].component_count = id + 1;178    }179}180 181kayan_table_has: proc(t: *kayan_table, id: u32) -> b32 = {182    return (t[0].signature & kayan_bit(id)) != 0;183}184 185// A table for a signature: one empty column per component in it, sized from186// the registry. Every component in the signature must be registered.187kayan_table_init: proc(w: *kayan_world, signature: u64) -> kayan_table = {188    t: kayan_table = {};189    t.signature = signature;190    for (id: u32 = 0; id < 64; id += 1) {191        if ((signature & kayan_bit(id)) != 0) {192            if (id >= w[0].component_count || w[0].infos[id] == null) {193                printfmt("kayan: signature {} uses component {}, which was never registered\n", signature, id);194                exit(1);195            }196            t.columns[id] = kayan_column_init(w[0].infos[id]);197        }198    }199    return t;200}201 202// Double the room in `entities` and in every column at once.203kayan_table_grow: proc(w: *kayan_world, t: *kayan_table) -> void = {204    capacity: u64 = t[0].capacity == 0 ? 4 : t[0].capacity * 2;205    entities: [*]kayan_entity = cast(memops_arena_push_zero(w[0].arena,206        sizeof(kayan_entity) * capacity, alignof(kayan_entity)), [*]kayan_entity);207    if (t[0].count > 0) {208        memcpy(entities[0]&, t[0].entities[0]&, sizeof(kayan_entity) * t[0].count);209    }210    t[0].entities = entities;211    for (id: u32 = 0; id < w[0].component_count; id += 1) {212        if (kayan_table_has(t, id)) {213            kayan_column_grow(w[0].arena, t[0].columns[id]&, t[0].count, capacity);214        }215    }216    t[0].capacity = capacity;217}218 219// A new row at the end, owned by `e`, with every component zeroed.220kayan_table_add_row: proc(w: *kayan_world, t: *kayan_table, e: kayan_entity) -> u64 = {221    if (t[0].count == t[0].capacity) {222        kayan_table_grow(w, t);223    }224    row: u64 = t[0].count;225    t[0].count += 1;226    t[0].entities[row] = e;227    for (id: u32 = 0; id < w[0].component_count; id += 1) {228        if (kayan_table_has(t, id)) {229            kayan_column_zero_row(t[0].columns[id]&, row);230        }231    }232    return row;233}234 235// 1.4's swap-remove, for every column: the last row is copied over `row`, and236// the slot of the entity that owned the last row is told where it went.237kayan_table_remove_row: proc(w: *kayan_world, t: *kayan_table, row: u64) -> void = {238    last: u64 = t[0].count - 1;239    if (row != last) {240        for (id: u32 = 0; id < w[0].component_count; id += 1) {241            if (kayan_table_has(t, id)) {242                kayan_column_copy_row(t[0].columns[id]&, row, last);243            }244        }245        moved: kayan_entity = t[0].entities[last];246        t[0].entities[row] = moved;247        vec<kayan_slot>at(w[0].slots&, cast(moved.index, u64))[0].row = cast(row, u32);248    }249    t[0].count = last;250}251 252// The typed view of one of the table's columns: T's rows, all of them in use.253// Asking for a component the table does not have is a bug, so it stops.254kayan_slice: proc<T>(t: *kayan_table) -> []T = {255    id: u32 = kayan_id_of<T>();256    if (!kayan_table_has(t, id)) {257        printfmt("kayan: the table has no column for component {}\n", id);258        exit(1);259    }260    return kayan_column_slice<T>(t[0].columns[id]&, t[0].count);261}262 263// A pointer to a table is good until the next table is made.264kayan_table_at: proc(w: *kayan_world, index: u32) -> *kayan_table = {265    return vec<kayan_table>at(w[0].tables&, cast(index, u64));266}267 268// The table for a signature: found if it exists, made if it does not. This is269// where archetypes come from.270kayan_table_for: proc(w: *kayan_world, signature: u64) -> u32 = {271    found: *u32 = hashmap<u64, u32>get(w[0].by_signature&, signature);272    if (found != null) {273        return found[0];274    }275    index: u32 = cast(w[0].tables.length, u32);276    _ = vec<kayan_table>append(w[0].arena, w[0].tables&, kayan_table_init(w, signature));277    _ = hashmap<u64, u32>put(w[0].arena, w[0].by_signature&, signature, index);278    return index;279}280 281// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------282// The world283// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------284 285kayan_world_init: proc(w: *kayan_world, arena: *memops_arena) -> void = {286    w[0] = {};287    w[0].arena = arena;288}289 290kayan_alive: proc(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity) -> b32 = {291    if (cast(e.index, u64) >= w[0].slots.length) {292        return false;293    }294    return vec<kayan_slot>at(w[0].slots&, cast(e.index, u64))[0].generation == e.generation;295}296 297// A new entity with the components in `signature`, all zeroed, in the table298// for that signature.299kayan_spawn: proc(w: *kayan_world, signature: u64) -> kayan_entity = {300    e: kayan_entity = {};301    if (!vec<u32>is_empty(w[0].free&)) {302        e.index = vec<u32>pop(w[0].free&);303    } else {304        e.index = cast(w[0].slots.length, u32);305        _ = vec<kayan_slot>append(w[0].arena, w[0].slots&, { .generation = 1 });306    }307    slot: *kayan_slot = vec<kayan_slot>at(w[0].slots&, cast(e.index, u64));308    e.generation = slot[0].generation;309    // kayan_table_for can make a table and move the others, so the table's310    // pointer is taken after it.311    table_index: u32 = kayan_table_for(w, signature);312    t: *kayan_table = kayan_table_at(w, table_index);313    slot[0].table = table_index;314    slot[0].row = cast(kayan_table_add_row(w, t, e), u32);315    w[0].live += 1;316    return e;317}318 319kayan_despawn: proc(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity) -> kayan_status = {320    if (!kayan_alive(w, e)) {321        return kayan_status.dead;322    }323    slot: *kayan_slot = vec<kayan_slot>at(w[0].slots&, cast(e.index, u64));324    kayan_table_remove_row(w, kayan_table_at(w, slot[0].table), cast(slot[0].row, u64));325    slot[0].generation += 1;326    _ = vec<u32>append(w[0].arena, w[0].free&, e.index);327    w[0].live -= 1;328    return kayan_status.ok;329}330 331// The components a live entity has: its table's signature. 0 for a dead one.332kayan_signature: proc(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity) -> u64 = {333    if (!kayan_alive(w, e)) {334        return 0;335    }336    return kayan_table_at(w, vec<kayan_slot>at(w[0].slots&, cast(e.index, u64))[0].table)[0].signature;337}338 339// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------340// Moving between tables341// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------342 343// The table an entity of table `from` moves to when it gains component `id`.344// The first time, it is found by signature, which can make the table; the345// answer is written on both tables, as from's add edge and the destination's346// remove edge, so neither direction is looked up again.347kayan_table_with: proc(w: *kayan_world, from: u32, id: u32) -> u32 = {348    edge: u32 = kayan_table_at(w, from)[0].add_edges[id];349    if (edge != 0) {350        return edge - 1;351    }352    to: u32 = kayan_table_for(w, kayan_table_at(w, from)[0].signature | kayan_bit(id));353    // kayan_table_for can move the tables, so both pointers are taken after it.354    kayan_table_at(w, from)[0].add_edges[id] = to + 1;355    kayan_table_at(w, to)[0].remove_edges[id] = from + 1;356    return to;357}358 359// The same for losing component `id`.360kayan_table_without: proc(w: *kayan_world, from: u32, id: u32) -> u32 = {361    edge: u32 = kayan_table_at(w, from)[0].remove_edges[id];362    if (edge != 0) {363        return edge - 1;364    }365    to: u32 = kayan_table_for(w, 371// Move a live entity to table `to_index`. The typed layer is for game code, which knows its types; this is401// for tools that work from reflect records instead.402kayan_get_bytes: proc(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity, id: u32) -> []u8 = {403    none: []u8 = {};404    if (!kayan_alive(w, e) || id >= w[0].component_count) {405        return none;406    }407    slot: *kayan_slot = vec<kayan_slot>at(w[0].slots&, cast(e.index, u64));408    t: *kayan_table = kayan_table_at(w, slot[0].table);409    if (!kayan_table_has(t, id)) {410        return none;411    }412    c: *kayan_column = t[0].columns[id]&;413    row: u64 = cast(slot[0].row, u64);414    all: []u8 = c[0].data[0..t[0].count * c[0].size];415    return all[row * c[0].size..(row + 1) * c[0].size];416}417 418// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------419// The typed layer420// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------421 422// e's T, or null if e is dead or has no T. Handle, slot, table, row, typed423// view: the same path as 1.4's get_position, for any component. The pointer is424// good until the next structural change, so use it now and keep the handle.425kayan_get: proc<T>(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity) -> *T = {426    if (!kayan_alive(w, e)) {427        return null;428    }429    slot: *kayan_slot = vec<kayan_slot>at(w[0].slots&, cast(e.index, u64));430    t: *kayan_table = kayan_table_at(w, slot[0].table);431    if (!kayan_table_has(t, kayan_id_of<T>())) {432        return null;433    }434    rows: []T = kayan_slice<T>(t);435    return rows[cast(slot[0].row, u64)]&;436}437 438kayan_has: proc<T>(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity) -> b32 = {439    return (kayan_signature(w, e) & kayan_mask_of<T>()) != 0;440}441 442// Write e's T. It must already have one: giving an entity a component it does443// not have changes its table, which is 2.6.444kayan_set: proc<T>(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity, value: T) -> kayan_status = {445    if (!kayan_alive(w, e)) {446        return kayan_status.dead;447    }448    p: *T = kayan_get<T>(w, e);449    if (p == null) {450        return kayan_status.missing;451    }452    p[0] = value;453    return kayan_status.ok;454}455 456// Give e a T. If it already has one, this is kayan_set; if not, it moves to457// the table with T and then sets it.458kayan_add: proc<T>(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity, value: T) -> kayan_status = {459    if (!kayan_alive(w, e)) {460        return kayan_status.dead;461    }462    if (!kayan_has<T>(w, e)) {463        from: u32 = vec<kayan_slot>at(w[0].slots&, cast(e.index, u64))[0].table;464        kayan_move(w, e, kayan_table_with(w, from, kayan_id_of<T>()));465    }466    return kayan_set<T>(w, e, value);467}468 469// Take e's T away, moving it to the table without T.470kayan_remove: proc<T>(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity) -> kayan_status = {471    if (!kayan_alive(w, e)) {472        return kayan_status.dead;473    }474    if (!kayan_has<T>(w, e)) {475        return kayan_status.missing;476    }477    from: u32 = vec<kayan_slot>at(w[0].slots&, cast(e.index, u64))[0].table;478    kayan_move(w, e, kayan_table_without(w, from, kayan_id_of<T>()));479    return kayan_status.ok;480}481 482// The invariant, over every table: each row belongs to a live entity whose483// slot points back at that table and row, and the rows of all tables add up to484// the live count.485kayan_verify: proc(w: *kayan_world) -> u64 = {486    problems: u64 = 0;487    rows: u64 = 0;488    for (ti: u64 = 0; ti < w[0].tables.length; ti += 1) {489        t: *kayan_table = kayan_table_at(w, cast(ti, u32));490        for (row: u64 = 0; row < t[0].count; row += 1) {491            e: kayan_entity = t[0].entities[row];492            if (!kayan_alive(w, e)) {493                printfmt("kayan_verify: table {} row {} holds dead entity {}:{}\n", ti, row, e.index, e.generation);494                problems += 1;495                continue;496            }497            slot: *kayan_slot = vec<kayan_slot>at(w[0].slots&, cast(e.index, u64));498            if (cast(slot[0].table, u64) != ti || cast(slot[0].row, u64) != row) {499                printfmt("kayan_verify: {}:{} is in table {} row {}, its slot says table {} row {}\n",500                    e.index, e.generation, ti, row, slot[0].table, slot[0].row);501                problems += 1;502            }503        }504        rows += t[0].count;505    }506    if (rows != w[0].live) {507        printfmt("kayan_verify: {} rows in tables, {} live entities\n", rows, w[0].live);508        problems += 1;509    }510    return problems;511}512 513kayan_print_signature: proc(w: *kayan_world, signature: u64) -> void = {514    printf("{");515    first: b32 = true;516    for (id: u32 = 0; id < w[0].component_count; id += 1) {517        if ((signature & kayan_bit(id)) != 0) {518            printf(first ? "%s" : " %s", w[0].infos[id][0].name);519            first = false;520        }521    }522    printf("}");523}524 525kayan_print_table: proc(w: *kayan_world, ti: u32) -> void = {526    t: *kayan_table = kayan_table_at(w, ti);527    printf("    table %u ", ti);528    kayan_print_signature(w, t[0].signature);529    printf(":");530    for (row: u64 = 0; row < t[0].count; row += 1) {531        printf(" %u:%u", t[0].entities[row].index, t[0].entities[row].generation);532    }533    printf("\n");534}535 536kayan_print_tables: proc(w: *kayan_world) -> void = {537    for (ti: u32 = 0; ti < cast(w[0].tables.length, u32); ti += 1) {538        kayan_print_table(w, ti);539    }540}541 542// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------543// The inspector: reflect records, no component types544// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------545 546kayan_indent: proc(depth: u32) -> void = {547    for (i: u32 = 0; i < depth; i += 1) {548        printf("    ");549    }550}551 552// One value of a builtin type, read from its bytes by its type's name.553kayan_print_builtin: proc(type_name: [*]const char, at: []const u8) -> void = {554    if (strcmp(type_name, "f32") == 0) {555        printf("%.2f", cast(cast(at[0]&, *const f32)[0], f64));556    } else if (strcmp(type_name, "u32") == 0) {557        printf("%u", cast(at[0]&, *const u32)[0]);558    } else if (strcmp(type_name, "i32") == 0) {559        printf("%d", cast(at[0]&, *const i32)[0]);560    } else {561        printf("<%s>", type_name);562    }563}564 565// Every field of a struct whose bytes are `base`, nested structs indented566// under their field. A field's bytes are cut from `base` by its offset and567// size, both from the reflect record.568kayan_print_fields: proc(type: *const reflect, base: []const u8, depth: u32) -> void = {569    fields: [*]const reflect_field = reflect_fields(type);570    for (i: u64 = 0; i < type[0].count; i += 1) {571        f: *const reflect_field = fields[i]&;572        if (reflect_field_has_attr(f, "hidden")) {573            continue;574        }575        at: []const u8 = base[f[0].offset..f[0].offset + f[0].size];576        kayan_indent(depth);577        printf("%s:", f[0].name);578        info: *const reflect = f[0].info;579        if (info != null && info[0].kind == reflect_kind_struct) {580            printf("\n");581            kayan_print_fields(info, at, depth + 1);582        } else {583            printf(" ");584            kayan_print_builtin(f[0].type, at);585            printf("\n");586        }587    }588}589 590kayan_inspect: proc(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity) -> void = {591    if (!kayan_alive(w, e)) {592        printfmt("{}:{} (dead)\n", e.index, e.generation);593        return;594    }595    printf("%u:%u ", e.index, e.generation);596    signature: u64 = kayan_signature(w, e);597    kayan_print_signature(w, signature);598    printf("\n");599    for (id: u32 = 0; id < w[0].component_count; id += 1) {600        if ((signature & kayan_bit(id)) != 0) {601            info: *const reflect = w[0].infos[id];602            printf("    %s\n", info[0].name);603            bytes: []u8 = kayan_get_bytes(w, e, id);604            kayan_print_fields(info, bytes, 2);605        }606    }607}608 609// Every table: rows in use out of room, and per column its row size and its610// bytes in use out of bytes allocated. The memory a table holds and does not611// use is the cost of doubling on growth.612kayan_print_layout: proc(w: *kayan_world) -> void = {613    for (ti: u32 = 0; ti < cast(w[0].tables.length, u32); ti += 1) {614        t: *kayan_table = kayan_table_at(w, ti);615        printf("table %u ", ti);616        kayan_print_signature(w, t[0].signature);617        printf(": %u rows, room for %u\n", cast(t[0].count, u32), cast(t[0].capacity, u32));618        for (id: u32 = 0; id < w[0].component_count; id += 1) {619            if (kayan_table_has(t, id)) {620                size: u64 = t[0].columns[id].size;621                printf("    %-9s %2u bytes a row, %4u of %4u bytes in use\n", w[0].infos[id][0].name, cast(size, u32),622                    cast(size * t[0].count, u32), cast(size * t[0].capacity, u32));623            }624        }625    }626}627 628// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------629// Queries630// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------631 632// The tables a system runs over: every table whose signature has all of `all`633// and none of `none`, kept by index. Tables are only ever added, at the end of634// w.tables, so the query remembers how many it has checked and, brought up to635// date, looks at the new ones only.636kayan_query: struct = {637    all: u64;638    none: u64;639    tables: vec<u32>;640    checked: u64;641}642 643kayan_query_init: proc(all: u64, none: u64) -> kayan_query = {644    q: kayan_query = {};645    q.all = all;646    q.none = none;647    return q;648}649 650kayan_matches: proc(signature: u64, all: u64, none: u64) -> b32 = {651    return (signature & all) == all && (signature & none) == 0;652}653 654// Check the tables made since the query last looked. With none new, this is655// one comparison, so call it before every walk.656kayan_query_update: proc(w: *kayan_world, q: *kayan_query) -> void = {657    for (ti: u64 = q[0].checked; ti < w[0].tables.length; ti += 1) {658        if (kayan_matches(kayan_table_at(w, cast(ti, u32))[0].signature, q[0].all, q[0].none)) {659            _ = vec<u32>append(w[0].arena, q[0].tables&, cast(ti, u32));660        }661    }662    q[0].checked = w[0].tables.length;663}664 665// The query's i-th table. Like any table pointer, good until a table is made.666kayan_query_table: proc(w: *kayan_world, q: *kayan_query, i: u64) -> *kayan_table = {667    return kayan_table_at(w, vec<u32>at(q[0].tables&, i)[0]);668}669 670// How many entities the query matches: the rows of its tables.671kayan_query_count: proc(w: *kayan_world, q: *kayan_query) -> u64 = {672    kayan_query_update(w, q);673    n: u64 = 0;674    for (i: u64 = 0; i < q[0].tables.length; i += 1) {675        n += kayan_query_table(w, q, i)[0].count;676    }677    return n;678}679 680kayan_print_query: proc(w: *kayan_world, name: [*]const char, q: *kayan_query) -> void = {681    kayan_query_update(w, q);682    printf("%s: all ", name);683    kayan_print_signature(w, q[0].all);684    printf(", none ");685    kayan_print_signature(w, q[0].none);686    printfmt("; tables: {}, entities: {}\n", q[0].tables.length, kayan_query_count(w, q));687    for (i: u64 = 0; i < q[0].tables.length; i += 1) {688        kayan_print_table(w, vec<u32>at(q[0].tables&, i)[0]);689    }690}691 692// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------693// The program694// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------695 696spawn_turret: proc(w: *kayan_world, x: f32, y: f32) -> kayan_entity = {697    e: kayan_entity = kayan_spawn(w, kayan_mask_of<position>() | kayan_mask_of<turret>());698    _ = kayan_set<position>(w, e, { .at = { .x = x, .y = y } });699    _ = kayan_set<turret>(w, e, { .cooldown = 0.5, .timer = 0.0 });700    return e;701}702 703spawn_drone: proc(w: *kayan_world, x: f32, y: f32) -> kayan_entity = {704    e: kayan_entity = kayan_spawn(w, kayan_mask_of<position>() | kayan_mask_of<velocity>() | kayan_mask_of<health>());705    _ = kayan_set<position>(w, e, { .at = { .x = x, .y = y } });706    _ = kayan_set<velocity>(w, e, { .per_second = { .x = -1.0, .y = 0.0 } });707    _ = kayan_set<health>(w, e, { .points = 100.0, .max = 100.0 });708    return e;709}710 711spawn_bullet: proc(w: *kayan_world, x: f32, y: f32) -> kayan_entity = {712    e: kayan_entity = kayan_spawn(w, kayan_mask_of<position>() | kayan_mask_of<velocity>()713        | kayan_mask_of<damage>() | kayan_mask_of<lifetime>());714    _ = kayan_set<position>(w, e, { .at = { .x = x, .y = y } });715    _ = kayan_set<velocity>(w, e, { .per_second = { .x = 8.0, .y = 0.0 } });716    _ = kayan_set<damage>(w, e, { .amount = 25.0 });717    _ = kayan_set<lifetime>(w, e, { .seconds = 2.0 });718    return e;719}720 721// Every entity a query matches, table by table, with its position.722print_positions: proc(w: *kayan_world, q: *kayan_query) -> void = {723    kayan_query_update(w, q);724    for (i: u64 = 0; i < q[0].tables.length; i += 1) {725        t: *kayan_table = kayan_query_table(w, q, i);726        ps: []position = kayan_slice<position>(t);727        for (row: u64 = 0; row < t[0].count; row += 1) {728            e: kayan_entity = t[0].entities[row];729            printf("    %u:%u at (%5.2f, %5.2f)\n", e.index, e.generation,730                cast(ps[row].at.x, f64), cast(ps[row].at.y, f64));731        }732    }733}734 735main: proc() -> i32 = {736    arena: memops_arena = {};737    memops_arena_initialize(arena&);738    w: kayan_world = {};739    kayan_world_init(w&, arena&);740    kayan_register(w&, kayan_id_of<position>(), position<>&);741    kayan_register(w&, kayan_id_of<velocity>(), velocity<>&);742    kayan_register(w&, kayan_id_of<health>(), health<>&);743    kayan_register(w&, kayan_id_of<damage>(), damage<>&);744    kayan_register(w&, kayan_id_of<lifetime>(), lifetime<>&);745    kayan_register(w&, kayan_id_of<turret>(), turret<>&);746    kayan_register(w&, kayan_id_of<burning>(), burning<>&);747 748    _ = spawn_turret(w&, 0.0, 0.0);749    _ = spawn_drone(w&, 20.0, 5.0);750    b: kayan_entity = spawn_drone(w&, 30.0, -5.0);751    _ = spawn_drone(w&, 40.0, 0.0);752    shot: kayan_entity = spawn_bullet(w&, 1.0, 0.0);753    printfmt("{} entities in {} tables:\n", w.live, w.tables.length);754    kayan_print_tables(w&);755 756    // Three queries. Build an ECS · part 3, systems · 3.2

Systems

ecs/src/3.systems/3.2.systems/systems.rin

3.1's movement loop had the shape of every system: bring a query up to date, then for each of its tables take the columns as slices and loop over the rows. This chapter names that shape and splits it in two:

  • the kernel: a plain loop over plain slices. It knows nothing about tables, entities or worlds. This is lessons 1 to 7: noalias, streaming, vectorization.
  • the system: a query, plus a small proc kayan calls on each table the query matches. It takes the table's columns and calls the kernel.

A frame runs the systems in order, each over all of its tables. The order is the schedule, and it's written down once, as data.

Step 1: the kernels

integrate: proc(ps: noalias []position, vs: []const velocity, dt: f32) -> void = {
    for (i: u64 = 0; i < ps.length; i += 1) {
        ps[i].at.x += vs[i].per_second.x * dt;
        ps[i].at.y += vs[i].per_second.y * dt;
    }
}

That's the whole thing, and it's the code you'd want to write if there were no ECS at all. Kernels are where you profile, read assembly and reach for SIMD (the lessons). Everything else in this course exists to hand them the right slices. burn and age look the same.

Step 2: what a system gets

kayan_iter: struct = {
    world: *kayan_world;
    table: *kayan_table;
    dt: f32;
}

kayan_system_proc: alias = *proc(it: *kayan_iter) -> void;

One struct instead of three parameters. It's the same idea as flecs' ecs_iter_t, and it has two practical reasons. Adding to it later (3.3 adds a field) changes no system's signature. And a system that uses only the table still uses its one parameter. rin compiles to C with -Wextra -Werror, and an unused parameter is an error there.

The system itself is the adapter:

move_system: proc(it: *kayan_iter) -> void = {
    integrate(kayan_slice<position>(it[0].table), kayan_slice<velocity>(it[0].table), it[0].dt);
}

Columns out, kernel in. No loop here: the kernel has it.

Step 3: a system is data

kayan_system: struct = {
    name: [*]const char;
    query: kayan_query;
    run: kayan_system_proc;
    tables: u64;
    rows: u64;
}

A name, a query, a proc pointer. tables and rows count the work, for the output. The schedule is an array of these:

    systems: [3]kayan_system = {};
    systems[0] = kayan_system_init("burn", kayan_mask_of<health>() | kayan_mask_of<burning>(), 0, burn_system);
    systems[1] = kayan_system_init("age", kayan_mask_of<lifetime>(), 0, age_system);
    systems[2] = kayan_system_init("move", kayan_mask_of<position>() | kayan_mask_of<velocity>(), 0, move_system);

Step 4: a frame

kayan_progress: proc(w: *kayan_world, systems: []kayan_system, dt: f32) -> void = {
    for (s: u64 = 0; s < systems.length; s += 1) {
        sys: *kayan_system = systems[s]&;
        kayan_query_update(w, sys[0].query&);
        for (i: u64 = 0; i < sys[0].query.tables.length; i += 1) {
            it: kayan_iter = {};
            it.world = w;
            it.table = kayan_query_table(w, sys[0].query&, i);
            it.dt = dt;
            if (it.table[0].count > 0) {
                sys[0].tables += 1;
                sys[0].rows += it.table[0].count;
                sys[0].run(it&);
            }
        }
    }
}

kayan_progress is flecs' name for the same thing. For each system in order, for each of its tables, one call. The game loop becomes:

    for (frame: u32 = 1; frame <= 8; frame += 1) {
        kayan_progress(w&, systems, dt);

Order is data flow

Systems run one after another, never interleaved, and each sees everything the earlier ones wrote this frame. So the order is a statement about data: a system that reads what another writes runs after it. Move before collide means bullets hit where they are now, not where they were. Damage before death means a drone dies in the frame its health hits zero, not the next. 3.4's schedule has nine systems, and each position in it is one of these decisions.

Bigger engines go further. Each system declares what it reads and writes, and the scheduler uses that to run systems that don't conflict at the same time, on other threads. Underneath, the order is still a list like this one.

Run it

the schedule, run in this order every frame:
burn: all {health burning}, none {}; tables: 1, entities: 1
    table 2 {position velocity health burning}: 2:1
age: all {lifetime}, none {}; tables: 1, entities: 3
    table 3 {position velocity damage lifetime}: 4:1 5:1 6:1
move: all {position velocity}, none {}; tables: 3, entities: 6
    table 1 {position velocity health}: 1:1 3:1
    table 2 {position velocity health burning}: 2:1
    table 3 {position velocity damage lifetime}: 4:1 5:1 6:1
...
after frame 8, 2.00 seconds:
    0:1 at ( 0.00,  0.00)
    1:1 at (18.00,  4.00)  health 100
    3:1 at (26.00, -4.00)  health 100
    2:1 at (22.00,  0.00)  health 84, burning
    4:1 at (17.00,  0.00)  lifetime -1.50
    5:1 at (17.00,  4.00)  lifetime -1.00
    6:1 at (17.00, -4.00)  lifetime -0.50

8 frames, one call per table per frame:
    burn called  8 times, over  8 rows
    age  called  8 times, over 24 rows
    move called 24 times, over 48 rows
3 bullets are out of time and still in the world

move made 24 calls in 8 frames, three tables a frame, and each call is one tight loop. Call overhead is per table, never per entity.

And the last line is the cliffhanger. Each bullet's lifetime ran out, and nothing removed it, because a system in this chapter changes values, never structure. Despawning from inside a system looks like a one-line fix. It isn't, and 3.3 shows why.

Try

  1. Swap burn and move in the schedule. Does anything change? Now think of a pair where it would.
  2. Add a heal system for drones that aren't burning (all {health}, none {burning}).
  3. Build in Release and find integrate in the assembly. Is it vectorized? (Lesson 1 shows how to look.)

This is270// where archetypes come from.271kayan_table_for: proc(w: *kayan_world, signature: u64) -> u32 = {272    found: *u32 = hashmap<u64, u32>get(w[0].by_signature&, signature);273    if (found != null) {274        return found[0];275    }276    index: u32 = cast(w[0].tables.length, u32);277    _ = vec<kayan_table>append(w[0].arena, w[0].tables&, kayan_table_init(w, signature));278    _ = hashmap<u64, u32>put(w[0].arena, w[0].by_signature&, signature, index);279    return index;280}281 282// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------283// The world284// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------285 286kayan_world_init: proc(w: *kayan_world, arena: *memops_arena) -> void = {287    w[0] = {};288    w[0].arena = arena;289}290 291kayan_alive: proc(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity) -> b32 = {292    if (cast(e.index, u64) >= w[0].slots.length) {293        return false;294    }295    return vec<kayan_slot>at(w[0].slots&, cast(e.index, u64))[0].generation == e.generation;296}297 298// A new entity with the components in `signature`, all zeroed, in the table299// for that signature.300kayan_spawn: proc(w: *kayan_world, signature: u64) -> kayan_entity = {301    e: kayan_entity = {};302    if (!vec<u32>is_empty(w[0].free&)) {303        e.index = vec<u32>pop(w[0].free&);304    } else {305        e.index = cast(w[0].slots.length, u32);306        _ = vec<kayan_slot>append(w[0].arena, w[0].slots&, { .generation = 1 });307    }308    slot: *kayan_slot = vec<kayan_slot>at(w[0].slots&, cast(e.index, u64));309    e.generation = slot[0].generation;310    // kayan_table_for can make a table and move the others, so the table's311    // pointer is taken after it.312    table_index: u32 = kayan_table_for(w, signature);313    t: *kayan_table = kayan_table_at(w, table_index);314    slot[0].table = table_index;315    slot[0].row = cast(kayan_table_add_row(w, t, e), u32);316    w[0].live += 1;317    return e;318}319 320kayan_despawn: proc(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity) -> kayan_status = {321    if (!kayan_alive(w, e)) {322        return kayan_status.dead;323    }324    slot: *kayan_slot = vec<kayan_slot>at(w[0].slots&, cast(e.index, u64));325    kayan_table_remove_row(w, kayan_table_at(w, slot[0].table), cast(slot[0].row, u64));326    slot[0].generation += 1;327    _ = vec<u32>append(w[0].arena, w[0].free&, e.index);328    w[0].live -= 1;329    return kayan_status.ok;330}331 332// The components a live entity has: its table's signature. 0 for a dead one.333kayan_signature: proc(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity) -> u64 = {334    if (!kayan_alive(w, e)) {335        return 0;336    }337    return kayan_table_at(w, vec<kayan_slot>at(w[0].slots&, cast(e.index, u64))[0].table)[0].signature;338}339 340// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------341// Moving between tables342// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------343 344// The table an entity of table `from` moves to when it gains component `id`.345// The first time, it is found by signature, which can make the table; the346// answer is written on both tables, as from's add edge and the destination's347// remove edge, so neither direction is looked up again.348kayan_table_with: proc(w: *kayan_world, from: u32, id: u32) -> u32 = {349    edge: u32 = kayan_table_at(w, from)[0].add_edges[id];350    if (edge != 0) {351        return edge - 1;352    }353    to: u32 = kayan_table_for(w, kayan_table_at(w, from)[0].signature | kayan_bit(id));354    // kayan_table_for can move the tables, so both pointers are taken after it.355    kayan_table_at(w, from)[0].add_edges[id] = to + 1;356    kayan_table_at(w, to)[0].remove_edges[id] = from + 1;357    return to;358}359 360// The same for losing component `id`.361kayan_table_without: proc(w: *kayan_world, from: u32, id: u32) -> u32 = {362    edge: u32 = kayan_table_at(w, from)[0].remove_edges[id];363    if (edge != 0) {364        return edge - 1;365    }366    to: u32 = kayan_table_for(w, kayan_table_at(w, from)[0].signature & ~kayan_bit(id));367    kayan_table_at(w, from)[0].remove_edges[id] = to + 1;368    kayan_table_at(w, to)[0].add_edges[id] = from + 1;369    return to;370}371 372// Move a live entity to table `to_index`. Components both tables have are373// copied, byte for byte; components only the new table has start zeroed;374// components only the old table has are dropped with its old row.375kayan_move: proc(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity, to_index: u32) -> void = {376    slot: *kayan_slot = vec<kayan_slot>at(w[0].slots&, cast(e.index, u64));377    from_index: u32 = slot[0].table;378    if (from_index == to_index) {379        return;380    }381    from: *kayan_table = kayan_table_at(w, from_index);382    to: *kayan_table = kayan_table_at(w, to_index);383    from_row: u64 = cast(slot[0].row, u64);384    to_row: u64 = kayan_table_add_row(w, to, e);385    for (id: u32 = 0; id < w[0].component_count; id += 1) {386        if (kayan_table_has(from, id) && kayan_table_has(to, id)) {387            memcpy(kayan_column_row(to[0].columns[id]&, to_row),388                kayan_column_row(from[0].columns[id]&, from_row), from[0].columns[id].size);389        }390    }391    kayan_table_remove_row(w, from, from_row);392    slot[0].table = to_index;393    slot[0].row = cast(to_row, u32);394}395 396// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------397// The byte layer, for tools398// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------399 400// e's component `id` as its bytes: an empty slice if e is dead or has no such401// component. The typed layer is for game code, which knows its types; this is402// for tools that work from reflect records instead.403kayan_get_bytes: proc(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity, id: u32) -> []u8 = {404    none: []u8 = {};405    if (!kayan_alive(w, e) || id >= w[0].component_count) {406        return none;407    }408    slot: *kayan_slot = vec<kayan_slot>at(w[0].slots&, cast(e.index, u64));409    t: *kayan_table = kayan_table_at(w, slot[0].table);410    if (!kayan_table_has(t, id)) {411        return none;412    }413    c: *kayan_column = t[0].columns[id]&;414    row: u64 = cast(slot[0].row, u64);415    all: []u8 = c[0].data[0..t[0].count * c[0].size];416    return all[row * c[0].size..(row + 1) * c[0].size];417}418 419// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------420// The typed layer421// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------422 423// e's T, or null if e is dead or has no T. Handle, slot, table, row, typed424// view: the same path as 1.4's get_position, for any component. The pointer is425// good until the next structural change, so use it now and keep the handle.426kayan_get: proc<T>(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity) -> *T = {427    if (!kayan_alive(w, e)) {428        return null;429    }430    slot: *kayan_slot = vec<kayan_slot>at(w[0].slots&, cast(e.index, u64));431    t: *kayan_table = kayan_table_at(w, slot[0].table);432    if (!kayan_table_has(t, kayan_id_of<T>())) {433        return null;434    }435    rows: []T = kayan_slice<T>(t);436    return rows[cast(slot[0].row, u64)]&;437}438 439kayan_has: proc<T>(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity) -> b32 = {440    return (kayan_signature(w, e) & kayan_mask_of<T>()) != 0;441}442 443// Write e's T. It must already have one: giving an entity a component it does444// not have changes its table, which is 2.6.445kayan_set: proc<T>(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity, value: T) -> kayan_status = {446    if (!kayan_alive(w, e)) {447        return kayan_status.dead;448    }449    p: *T = kayan_get<T>(w, e);450    if (p == null) {451        return kayan_status.missing;452    }453    p[0] = value;454    return kayan_status.ok;455}456 457// Give e a T. If it already has one, this is kayan_set; if not, it moves to458// the table with T and then sets it.459kayan_add: proc<T>(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity, value: T) -> kayan_status = {460    if (!kayan_alive(w, e)) {461        return kayan_status.dead;462    }463    if (!kayan_has<T>(w, e)) {464        from: u32 = vec<kayan_slot>at(w[0].slots&, cast(e.index, u64))[0].table;465        kayan_move(w, e, kayan_table_with(w, from, kayan_id_of<T>()));466    }467    return kayan_set<T>(w, e, value);468}469 470// Take e's T away, moving it to the table without T.471kayan_remove: proc<T>(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity) -> kayan_status = {472    if (!kayan_alive(w, e)) {473        return kayan_status.dead;474    }475    if (!kayan_has<T>(w, e)) {476        return kayan_status.missing;477    }478    from: u32 = vec<kayan_slot>at(w[0].slots&, cast(e.index, u64))[0].table;479    kayan_move(w, e, kayan_table_without(w, from, kayan_id_of<T>()));480    return kayan_status.ok;481}482 483// The invariant, over every table: each row belongs to a live entity whose484// slot points back at that table and row, and the rows of all tables add up to485// the live count.486kayan_verify: proc(w: *kayan_world) -> u64 = {487    problems: u64 = 0;488    rows: u64 = 0;489    for (ti: u64 = 0; ti < w[0].tables.length; ti += 1) {490        t: *kayan_table = kayan_table_at(w, cast(ti, u32));491        for (row: u64 = 0; row < t[0].count; row += 1) {492            e: kayan_entity = t[0].entities[row];493            if (!kayan_alive(w, e)) {494                printfmt("kayan_verify: table {} row {} holds dead entity {}:{}\n", ti, row, e.index, e.generation);495                problems += 1;496                continue;497            }498            slot: *kayan_slot = vec<kayan_slot>at(w[0].slots&, cast(e.index, u64));499            if (cast(slot[0].table, u64) != ti || cast(slot[0].row, u64) != row) {500                printfmt("kayan_verify: {}:{} is in table {} row {}, its slot says table {} row {}\n",501                    e.index, e.generation, ti, row, slot[0].table, slot[0].row);502                problems += 1;503            }504        }505        rows += t[0].count;506    }507    if (rows != w[0].live) {508        printfmt("kayan_verify: {} rows in tables, {} live entities\n", rows, w[0].live);509        problems += 1;510    }511    return problems;512}513 514kayan_print_signature: proc(w: *kayan_world, signature: u64) -> void = {515    printf("{");516    first: b32 = true;517    for (id: u32 = 0; id < w[0].component_count; id += 1) {518        if ((signature & kayan_bit(id)) != 0) {519            printf(first ? "%s" : " %s", w[0].infos[id][0].name);520            first = false;521        }522    }523    printf("}");524}525 526kayan_print_table: proc(w: *kayan_world, ti: u32) -> void = {527    t: *kayan_table = kayan_table_at(w, ti);528    printf("    table %u ", ti);529    kayan_print_signature(w, t[0].signature);530    printf(":");531    for (row: u64 = 0; row < t[0].count; row += 1) {532        printf(" %u:%u", t[0].entities[row].index, t[0].entities[row].generation);533    }534    printf("\n");535}536 537kayan_print_tables: proc(w: *kayan_world) -> void = {538    for (ti: u32 = 0; ti < cast(w[0].tables.length, u32); ti += 1) {539        kayan_print_table(w, ti);540    }541}542 543// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------544// The inspector: reflect records, no component types545// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------546 547kayan_indent: proc(depth: u32) -> void = {548    for (i: u32 = 0; i < depth; i += 1) {549        printf("    ");550    }551}552 553// One value of a builtin type, read from its bytes by its type's name.554kayan_print_builtin: proc(type_name: [*]const char, at: []const u8) -> void = {555    if (strcmp(type_name, "f32") == 0) {556        printf("%.2f", cast(cast(at[0]&, *const f32)[0], f64));557    } else if (strcmp(type_name, "u32") == 0) {558        printf("%u", cast(at[0]&, *const u32)[0]);559    } else if (strcmp(type_name, "i32") == 0) {560        printf("%d", cast(at[0]&, *const i32)[0]);561    } else {562        printf("<%s>", type_name);563    }564}565 566// Every field of a struct whose bytes are `base`, nested structs indented567// under their field. A field's bytes are cut from `base` by its offset and568// size, both from the reflect record.569kayan_print_fields: proc(type: *const reflect, base: []const u8, depth: u32) -> void = {570    fields: [*]const reflect_field = reflect_fields(type);571    for (i: u64 = 0; i < type[0].count; i += 1) {572        f: *const reflect_field = fields[i]&;573        if (reflect_field_has_attr(f, "hidden")) {574            continue;575        }576        at: []const u8 = base[f[0].offset..f[0].offset + f[0].size];577        kayan_indent(depth);578        printf("%s:", f[0].name);579        info: *const reflect = f[0].info;580        if (info != null && info[0].kind == reflect_kind_struct) {581            printf("\n");582            kayan_print_fields(info, at, depth + 1);583        } else {584            printf(" ");585            kayan_print_builtin(f[0].type, at);586            printf("\n");587        }588    }589}590 591kayan_inspect: proc(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity) -> void = {592    if (!kayan_alive(w, e)) {593        printfmt("{}:{} (dead)\n", e.index, e.generation);594        return;595    }596    printf("%u:%u ", e.index, e.generation);597    signature: u64 = kayan_signature(w, e);598    kayan_print_signature(w, signature);599    printf("\n");600    for (id: u32 = 0; id < w[0].component_count; id += 1) {601        if ((signature & kayan_bit(id)) != 0) {602            info: *const reflect = w[0].infos[id];603            printf("    %s\n", info[0].name);604            bytes: []u8 = kayan_get_bytes(w, e, id);605            kayan_print_fields(info, bytes, 2);606        }607    }608}609 610// Every table: rows in use out of room, and per column its row size and its611// bytes in use out of bytes allocated. The memory a table holds and does not612// use is the cost of doubling on growth.613kayan_print_layout: proc(w: *kayan_world) -> void = {614    for (ti: u32 = 0; ti < cast(w[0].tables.length, u32); ti += 1) {615        t: *kayan_table = kayan_table_at(w, ti);616        printf("table %u ", ti);617        kayan_print_signature(w, t[0].signature);618        printf(": %u rows, room for %u\n", cast(t[0].count, u32), cast(t[0].capacity, u32));619        for (id: u32 = 0; id < w[0].component_count; id += 1) {620            if (kayan_table_has(t, id)) {621                size: u64 = t[0].columns[id].size;622                printf("    %-9s %2u bytes a row, %4u of %4u bytes in use\n", w[0].infos[id][0].name, cast(size, u32),623                    cast(size * t[0].count, u32), cast(size * t[0].capacity, u32));624            }625        }626    }627}628 629// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------630// Queries631// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------632 633// The tables a system runs over: every table whose signature has all of `all`634// and none of `none`, kept by index. Tables are only ever added, at the end of635// w.tables, so the query remembers how many it has checked and, brought up to636// date, looks at the new ones only.637kayan_query: struct = {638    all: u64;639    none: u64;640    tables: vec<u32>;641    checked: u64;642}643 644kayan_query_init: proc(all: u64, none: u64) -> kayan_query = {645    q: kayan_query = {};646    q.all = all;647    q.none = none;648    return q;649}650 651kayan_matches: proc(signature: u64, all: u64, none: u64) -> b32 = {652    return (signature & all) == all && (signature & none) == 0;653}654 655// Check the tables made since the query last looked. With none new, this is656// one comparison, so call it before every walk.657kayan_query_update: proc(w: *kayan_world, q: *kayan_query) -> void = {658    for (ti: u64 = q[0].checked; ti < w[0].tables.length; ti += 1) {659        if (kayan_matches(kayan_table_at(w, cast(ti, u32))[0].signature, q[0].all, q[0].none)) {660            _ = vec<u32>append(w[0].arena, q[0].tables&, cast(ti, u32));661        }662    }663    q[0].checked = w[0].tables.length;664}665 666// The query's i-th table. Like any table pointer, good until a table is made.667kayan_query_table: proc(w: *kayan_world, q: *kayan_query, i: u64) -> *kayan_table = {668    return kayan_table_at(w, vec<u32>at(q[0].tables&, i)[0]);669}670 671// How many entities the query matches: the rows of its tables.672kayan_query_count: proc(w: *kayan_world, q: *kayan_query) -> u64 = {673    kayan_query_update(w, q);674    n: u64 = 0;675    for (i: u64 = 0; i < q[0].tables.length; i += 1) {676        n += kayan_query_table(w, q, i)[0].count;677    }678    return n;679}680 681kayan_print_query: proc(w: *kayan_world, name: [*]const char, q: *kayan_query) -> void = {682    kayan_query_update(w, q);683    printf("%s: all ", name);684    kayan_print_signature(w, q[0].all);685    printf(", none ");686    kayan_print_signature(w, q[0].none);687    printfmt("; tables: {}, entities: {}\n", q[0].tables.length, kayan_query_count(w, q));688    for (i: u64 = 0; i < q[0].tables.length; i += 1) {689        kayan_print_table(w, vec<u32>at(q[0].tables&, i)[0]);690    }691}692 693// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------694// Systems695// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------696 697// What a system gets for each table it runs on: the world, the table, and the698// frame's time step. One struct rather than three parameters, so that adding699// to it later changes no system's signature.700kayan_iter: struct = {701    world: *kayan_world;702    table: *kayan_table;703    dt: f32;704}705 706kayan_system_proc: alias = *proc(it: *kayan_iter) -> void;707 708// A system: a name, the query that finds its tables, and the proc run on each709// of those tables that has rows. `tables` and `rows` count what it has run710// over.711kayan_system: struct = {712    name: [*]const char;713    query: kayan_query;714    run: kayan_system_proc;715    tables: u64;716    rows: u64;717}718 719kayan_system_init: proc(name: [*]const char, all: u64, none: u64, run: kayan_system_proc) -> kayan_system = {720    s: kayan_system = {};721    s.name = name;722    s.query = kayan_query_init(all, none);723    s.run = run;724    return s;725}726 727// One frame: every system in order, each over every table it matches that has728// rows. A system sees everything the systems before it wrote this frame.729kayan_progress: proc(w: *kayan_world, systems: []kayan_system, dt: f32) -> void = {730    for (s: u64 = 0; s < systems.length; s += 1) {731        sys: *kayan_system = systems[s]&;732        kayan_query_update(w, sys[0].query&);733        for (i: u64 = 0; i < sys[0].query.tables.length; i += 1) {734            it: kayan_iter = {};735            it.world = w;736            it.table = kayan_query_table(w, sys[0].query&, i);737            it.dt = dt;738            if (it.table[0].count > 0) {739                sys[0].tables += 1;740                sys[0].rows += it.table[0].count;741                sys[0].run(it&);742            }743        }744    }745}746 747kayan_print_schedule: proc(w: *kayan_world, systems: []kayan_system) -> void = {748    for (s: u64 = 0; s < systems.length; s += 1) {749        kayan_print_query(w, systems[s].name, systems[s].query&);750    }751}752 753// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------754// The program755// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------756 757// Kernels: plain loops over plain slices, with components for elements.758// noalias on what each one writes, as in lessons 1 to 7.759integrate: proc(ps: noalias []position, vs: []const velocity, dt: f32) -> void = {760    for (i: u64 = 0; i < ps.length; i += 1) {761        ps[i].at.x += vs[i].per_second.x * dt;762        ps[i].at.y += vs[i].per_second.y * dt;763    }764}765 766burn: proc(hs: noalias []health, fires: []const burning, dt: f32) -> void = {767    for (i: u64 = 0; i < hs.length; i += 1) {768        hs[i].points -= fires[i].per_second * dt;769    }770}771 772age: proc(ls: noalias []lifetime, dt: f32) -> void = {773    for (i: u64 = 0; i < ls.length; i += 1) {774        ls[i].seconds -= dt;775    }776}777 778// Systems: the table's columns, handed to a kernel.779move_system: proc(it: *kayan_iter) -> void = {780    integrate(kayan_slice<position>(it[0].table), kayan_slice<velocity>(it[0].table), it[0].dt);781}782 783burn_system: proc(it: *kayan_iter) -> void = {784    burn(kayan_slice<health>(it[0].table), kayan_slice<burning>(it[0].table), it[0].dt);785}786 787age_system: proc(it: *kayan_iter) -> void = {788    age(kayan_slice<lifetime>(it[0].table), it[0].dt);789}790 791spawn_turret: proc(w: *kayan_world, x: f32, y: f32) -> kayan_entity = {792    e: kayan_entity = kayan_spawn(w, kayan_mask_of<position>() | kayan_mask_of<turret>());793    _ = 806spawn_bullet: proc(w: *kayan_world, x: f32, y: f32, seconds: f32) -> kayan_entity = {807    e: kayan_entity = kayan_spawn(w, kayan_mask_of<position>() | kayan_mask_of<velocity>()808        | cares about.817print_state: proc(w: *kayan_world) -> void = {818    for (ti: u32 = 0; ti < cast(w[0].tables.length, u32); ti += 1) {819        t: *kayan_table = kayan_table_at(w, ti);820        for (row: u64 = 0; row < t[0].count; row += 1) {821            e: kayan_entity = t[0].entities[row];822            p: *position = kayan_get<position>(w, e);823            printf("    %u:%u at (%5.2f, %5.2f)", e.index, e.generation, cast(p[0].at.x, f64), cast(p[0].at.y, f64));824            h: *health = kayan_get<health>(w, e);825            if (h != null) {826                printf("  health Build an ECS · part 3, systems · 3.3

Commands

ecs/src/3.systems/3.3.commands/commands.rin

3.2's systems change values, never structure, so bullets whose time ran out stay in the world. The obvious fix is to despawn them from inside the system. It's wrong, and seeing exactly why is most of this chapter.

Step 1: the bug

expire_now_system: proc(it: *kayan_iter) -> void = {
    t: *kayan_table = it[0].table;
    ls: []lifetime = kayan_slice<lifetime>(t);
    for (row: u64 = 0; row < t[0].count; row += 1) {
        if (ls[row].seconds <= 0.0) {
            _ = kayan_despawn(it[0].world, t[0].entities[row]);
        }
    }
}

Four bullets, three of them out of time:

1. an expire system that despawns as it goes
    lifetimes:  0:1 0.00  1:1 1.00  2:1 0.00  3:1 0.00
after one frame:
    lifetimes:  3:1 0.00  1:1 1.00
kayan_verify: 0 problems. The world is fine; the loop missed one.

Row by row:

row 0: 0:1 is out of time. Despawn: the last row, 3:1, moves into row 0.
row 1: 1:1 has time left.
row 2: 2:1 is out of time. Despawn: it's the last row, so nothing moves.
row 3: the table has 2 rows now. Stop.

3:1 moved into row 0, which the loop had already passed, so it was never looked at. The world is perfectly consistent (kayan_verify agrees). The loop is what's wrong: a despawn swap-removes from the table the loop is walking.

Walking backwards fixes this case (lesson 2 does it), because the row that moves in has already been looked at. But it doesn't fix the general problem:

  • Adding or removing a component moves the entity to another table. If the query matches that table too and visits it later, the entity is processed twice.
  • If that table is new, making it can grow w.tables and move every table. The t the loop is holding then points at the old copy, which the arena still owns, so nothing crashes and every write after that is lost. This is 2.4's bug, from inside a loop.
  • One system's despawn can land in a table another system is halfway through, if a system despawns entities it found through a second query.

Step 2: record now, apply later

So a system doesn't change structure. It records a command saying what should change, and the world applies every command after the frame's last system:

during the frame   values change; tables, rows and pointers do not
after the frame    spawns, despawns, adds and removes, in order
kayan_command_kind: enum = {
    spawn,
    despawn,
    add,
    remove,
}

kayan_command: struct = {
    kind: kayan_command_kind;
    entity: kayan_entity;
    spawn: u32;
    id: u32;
    signature: u64;
    value: []u8;
}

A command names the entity, and for an add or remove the component id. An add carries its value as bytes. The bytes, and the list of commands, live in a frame arena the world owns:

    frame: memops_arena;
    commands: vec<kayan_command>;

After the commands are applied, memops_arena_clear drops all of them at once, whatever they were.

Step 3: recording

The typed procs a system calls copy the value into the frame arena and append a command:

kayan_defer_value: proc<T>(w: *kayan_world, value: T) -> []u8 = {
    data: [*]u8 = cast(memops_arena_push(w[0].frame&, sizeof(T), alignof(T)), [*]u8);
    memcpy(data[0]&, value&, sizeof(T));
    return data[0..sizeof(T)];
}
kayan_defer_add: proc<T>(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity, value: T) -> void = {
    _ = kayan_defer(w, { .kind = kayan_command_kind.add, .entity = e, .id = kayan_id_of<T>(),
        .value = kayan_defer_value<T>(w, value) });
}

The fixed expire system is the broken one with one word changed:

expire_system: proc(it: *kayan_iter) -> void = {
    ls: []lifetime = kayan_slice<lifetime>(it[0].table);
    es: []kayan_entity = kayan_entities(it[0].table);
    for (row: u64 = 0; row < es.length; row += 1) {
        if (ls[row].seconds <= 0.0) {
            kayan_defer_despawn(it[0].world, es[row]);
        }
    }
}

Now the table doesn't change while the loop runs, so the loop can take the entities as a slice up front, like any other column.

Step 4: applying, by id

Commands hold bytes and ids, not types. So applying an add needs 2.6's add by id:

kayan_add_id: proc(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity, id: u32, value: []const u8) -> kayan_status = {

It's the same move-then-write as before, with the write a memcpy of the value's bytes into the row. Once that exists, the typed kayan_add<T> from 2.6 shrinks to a one-line wrapper. That's the pattern from the start of the course: byte fiddling written once, a type-safe generic layer on top.

kayan_add: proc<T>(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity, value: T) -> kayan_status = {
    bytes: [*]const u8 = cast(value&, [*]const u8);
    return kayan_add_id(w, e, kayan_id_of<T>(), bytes[0..sizeof(T)]);
}

kayan_flush walks the list in order and applies each command. It's called at the end of kayan_progress:

    kayan_flush(w);
}

Step 5: commands that arrive too late

By the time a command is applied, its entity may be gone. The usual case is two systems both asking to despawn the same thing. Applying in order handles that for free: the first despawn works, and the second finds a dead handle. Part 1's generations make that check one comparison:

        if (status == kayan_status.ok) {
            w[0].applied += 1;
        } else {
            w[0].skipped += 1;
        }

Step 6: spawning from a system

A turret firing is a spawn in the middle of a frame. The new entity doesn't exist until the commands are applied, so there's no handle to give its components to. kayan_defer_spawn returns a pending spawn instead: the spawn command's place in the list. Components are given to that:

            shot: kayan_pending = kayan_defer_spawn(it[0].world, bullet_signature());
            kayan_pending_set<position>(it[0].world, shot, ps[row]);
            kayan_pending_set<velocity>(it[0].world, shot, { .per_second = { .x = 8.0, .y = 0.0 } });
            kayan_pending_set<damage>(it[0].world, shot, { .amount = 25.0 });
            kayan_pending_set<lifetime>(it[0].world, shot, { .seconds = 2.0 });

When the flush reaches the spawn, it makes the entity and writes the handle into the command. The adds after it look the handle up there. The bullet is spawned with its full signature, so the adds land in the table it's already in: no moves. And it doesn't move until the next frame, because no system ran over it this one.

Step 7: a system with two queries

A bullet that reaches a target damages it. The hit system walks the bullets (its own query) and, for each, the targets (a second query). It reaches the second query through a new field, ctx, which kayan passes through untouched:

    targets: *kayan_query = cast(it[0].ctx, *kayan_query);

The damage is a value, so it's written now. The bullet's despawn is structure, so it's recorded. Walking a second query in the middle of a frame is safe because of commands: no table is made or moved until the frame is over.

In frame 4, bullet 4:1 is close enough to both targets. Both lose 25, and both hits record a despawn. The first applies; the second finds 4:1 already dead and is skipped. In frame 5 the next bullet gets number 4 back with generation 2: Part 1, working.

17 commands, for three bullets and two despawns: each spawn is five, the spawn and its four components.

Try

  1. In expire_now_system, loop to ls.length instead of t[0].count. Now all three get despawned. Work out why. (Hint: what's in the rows past the end of the table?) Is that loop correct?
  2. Write a system that adds burning directly (not deferred) to every target it walks. Count how many times it visits each entity.
  3. Flush after each system instead of after the frame. What does that change about what later systems see? (flecs calls these sync points.)
