id < w[0].component_count; id += 1) {244        if (kayan_table_has(t, id)) {245            kayan_column_grow(w[0].arena, t[0].columns[id]&, t[0].count, capacity);246        }247    }248    t[0].capacity = capacity;249}250 251// A new row at the end, owned by `e`, with every component zeroed.252kayan_table_add_row: proc(w: *kayan_world, t: *kayan_table, e: kayan_entity) -> u64 = {253    if (t[0].count == t[0].capacity) {254        kayan_table_grow(w, t);255    }256    row: u64 = t[0].count;257    t[0].count += 1;258    t[0].entities[row] = e;259    for (id: u32 = 0; id < w[0].component_count; id += 1) {260        if (kayan_table_has(t, id)) {261            kayan_column_zero_row(t[0].columns[id]&, row);262        }263    }264    return row;265}266 267// 1.4's swap-remove, for every column: the last row is copied over `row`, and268// the slot of the entity that owned the last row is told where it went.269kayan_table_remove_row: proc(w: *kayan_world, t: *kayan_table, row: u64) -> void = {270    last: u64 = t[0].count - 1;271    if (row != last) {272        for (id: u32 = 0; id < w[0].component_count; id += 1) {273            if (kayan_table_has(t, id)) {274                kayan_column_copy_row(t[0].columns[id]&, row, last);275            }276        }277        moved: kayan_entity = t[0].entities[last];278        t[0].entities[row] = moved;279        vec<kayan_slot>at(w[0].slots&, cast(moved.index, u64))[0].row = cast(row, u32);280    }281    t[0].count = last;282}283 284// The typed view of one of the table's columns: T's rows, all of them in use.285// Asking for a component the table does not have is a bug, so it stops.286kayan_slice: proc<T>(t: *kayan_table) -> []T = {287    id: u32 = kayan_id_of<T>();288    if (!kayan_table_has(t, id)) {289        printfmt("kayan: the table has no column for component {}\n", id);290        exit(1);291    }292    return kayan_column_slice<T>(t[0].columns[id]&, t[0].count);293}294 295// Who owns each of the table's rows.296kayan_entities: proc(t: *kayan_table) -> []kayan_entity = {297    return t[0].entities[0..t[0].count];298}299 300// A pointer to a table is good until the next table is made.301kayan_table_at: proc(w: *kayan_world, index: u32) -> *kayan_table = {302    return vec<kayan_table>at(w[0].tables&, cast(index, u64));303}304 305// The table for a signature: found if it exists, made if it does not. This is306// where archetypes come from.307kayan_table_for: proc(w: *kayan_world, signature: u64) -> u32 = {308    found: *u32 = hashmap<u64, u32>get(w[0].by_signature&, signature);309    if (found != null) {310        return found[0];311    }312    index: u32 = cast(w[0].tables.length, u32);313    _ = vec<kayan_table>append(w[0].arena, w[0].tables&, kayan_table_init(w, signature));314    _ = hashmap<u64, u32>put(w[0].arena, w[0].by_signature&, signature, index);315    return index;316}317 318// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------319// The world320// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------321 322kayan_world_init: proc(w: *kayan_world, arena: *memops_arena) -> void = {323    w[0] = {};324    w[0].arena = arena;325    // A frame's commands are small: 256 MB of address space is plenty.326    memops_arena_initialize(w[0].frame&, 0x10000000);327}328 329kayan_alive: proc(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity) -> b32 = {330    if (cast(e.index, u64) >= w[0].slots.length) {331        return false;332    }333    return vec<kayan_slot>at(w[0].slots&, cast(e.index, u64))[0].generation == e.generation;334}335 336// A new entity with the components in `signature`, all zeroed, in the table337// for that signature.338kayan_spawn: proc(w: *kayan_world, signature: u64) -> kayan_entity = {339    e: kayan_entity = {};340    if (!vec<u32>is_empty(w[0].free&)) {341        e.index = vec<u32>pop(w[0].free&);342    } else {343        e.index = cast(w[0].slots.length, u32);344        _ = vec<kayan_slot>append(w[0].arena, w[0].slots&, { .generation = 1 });345    }346    slot: *kayan_slot = vec<kayan_slot>at(w[0].slots&, cast(e.index, u64));347    e.generation = slot[0].generation;348    // kayan_table_for can make a table and move the others, so the table's349    // pointer is taken after it.350    table_index: u32 = kayan_table_for(w, signature);351    t: *kayan_table = kayan_table_at(w, table_index);352    slot[0].table = table_index;353    slot[0].row = cast(kayan_table_add_row(w, t, e), u32);354    w[0].live += 1;355    return e;356}357 358kayan_despawn: proc(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity) -> kayan_status = {359    if (!kayan_alive(w, e)) {360        return kayan_status.dead;361    }362    slot: *kayan_slot = vec<kayan_slot>at(w[0].slots&, cast(e.index, u64));363    kayan_table_remove_row(w, kayan_table_at(w, slot[0].table), cast(slot[0].row, u64));364    slot[0].generation += 1;365    _ = vec<u32>append(w[0].arena, w[0].free&, e.index);366    w[0].live -= 1;367    return kayan_status.ok;368}369 370// The components a live entity has: its table's signature. 0 for a dead one.371kayan_signature: proc(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity) -> u64 = {372    if (!kayan_alive(w, e)) {373        return 0;374    }375    return kayan_table_at(w, vec<kayan_slot>at(w[0].slots&, cast(e.index, u64))[0].table)[0].signature;376}377 378// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------379// Moving between tables380// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------381 382// The table an entity of table `from` moves to when it gains component `id`.383// The first time, it is found by signature, which can make the table; the384// answer is written on both tables, as from's add edge and the destination's385// remove edge, so neither direction is looked up again.386kayan_table_with: proc(w: *kayan_world, from: u32, id: u32) -> u32 = {387    edge: u32 = kayan_table_at(w, from)[0].add_edges[id];388    if (edge != 0) {389        return edge - 1;390    }391    to: u32 = kayan_table_for(w, kayan_table_at(w, from)[0].signature | kayan_bit(id));392    // kayan_table_for can move the tables, so both pointers are taken after it.393    kayan_table_at(w, from)[0].add_edges[id] = to + 1;394    kayan_table_at(w, to)[0].remove_edges[id] = from + 1;395    return to;396}397 398// The same for losing component `id`.399kayan_table_without: proc(w: *kayan_world, from: u32, id: u32) -> u32 = {400    edge: u32 = kayan_table_at(w, from)[0].remove_edges[id];401    if (edge != 0) {402        return edge - 1;403    }404    to: u32 = kayan_table_for(w, kayan_table_at(w, from)[0].signature & ~kayan_bit(id));405    kayan_table_at(w, from)[0].remove_edges[id] = to + 1;406    kayan_table_at(w, to)[0].add_edges[id] = from + 1;407    return to;408}409 410// Move a live entity to table `to_index`. Components both tables have are411// copied, byte for byte; components only the new table has start zeroed;412// components only the old table has are dropped with its old row.413kayan_move: proc(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity, to_index: u32) -> void = {414    slot: *kayan_slot = vec<kayan_slot>at(w[0].slots&, cast(e.index, u64));415    from_index: u32 = slot[0].table;416    if (from_index == to_index) {417        return;418    }419    from: *kayan_table = kayan_table_at(w, from_index);420    to: *kayan_table = kayan_table_at(w, to_index);421    from_row: u64 = cast(slot[0].row, u64);422    to_row: u64 = kayan_table_add_row(w, to, e);423    for (id: u32 = 0; id < w[0].component_count; id += 1) {424        if (kayan_table_has(from, id) && kayan_table_has(to, id)) {425            memcpy(kayan_column_row(to[0].columns[id]&, to_row),426                kayan_column_row(from[0].columns[id]&, from_row), from[0].columns[id].size);427        }428    }429    kayan_table_remove_row(w, from, from_row);430    slot[0].table = to_index;431    slot[0].row = cast(to_row, u32);432}433 434// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------435// The byte layer, for tools436// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------437 438// e's component `id` as its bytes: an empty slice if e is dead or has no such439// component. The typed layer is for game code, which knows its types; this is440// for tools that work from reflect records instead.441kayan_get_bytes: proc(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity, id: u32) -> []u8 = {442    none: []u8 = {};443    if (!kayan_alive(w, e) || id >= w[0].component_count) {444        return none;445    }446    slot: *kayan_slot = vec<kayan_slot>at(w[0].slots&, cast(e.index, u64));447    t: *kayan_table = kayan_table_at(w, slot[0].table);448    if (!kayan_table_has(t, id)) {449        return none;450    }451    c: *kayan_column = t[0].columns[id]&;452    row: u64 = cast(slot[0].row, u64);453    all: []u8 = c[0].data[0..t[0].count * c[0].size];454    return all[row * c[0].size..(row + 1) * c[0].size];455}456 457// Give e component `id`, with `value` for its bytes: 2.6's add, by id instead458// of by type, because a command holds its value as bytes.459kayan_add_id: proc(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity, id: u32, value: []const u8) -> kayan_status = {460    if (!kayan_alive(w, e)) {461        return kayan_status.dead;462    }463    from: u32 = vec<kayan_slot>at(w[0].slots&, cast(e.index, u64))[0].table;464    if (!kayan_table_has(kayan_table_at(w, from), id)) {465        kayan_move(w, e, kayan_table_with(w, from, id));466    }467    bytes: []u8 = kayan_get_bytes(w, e, id);468    if (value.length != bytes.length) {469        printfmt("kayan: a {}-byte value for a component of {} bytes\n", value.length, bytes.length);470        exit(1);471    }472    memcpy(bytes[0]&, value[0]&, bytes.length);473    return kayan_status.ok;474}475 476kayan_remove_id: proc(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity, id: u32) -> kayan_status = {477    if (!kayan_alive(w, e)) {478        return kayan_status.dead;479    }480    from: u32 = vec<kayan_slot>at(w[0].slots&, cast(e.index, u64))[0].table;481    if (!kayan_table_has(kayan_table_at(w, from), id)) {482        return kayan_status.missing;483    }484    kayan_move(w, e, kayan_table_without(w, from, id));485    return kayan_status.ok;486}487 488// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------489// The typed layer490// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------491 492// e's T, or null if e is dead or has no T. Handle, slot, table, row, typed493// view: the same path as 1.4's get_position, for any component. The pointer is494// good until the next structural change, so use it now and keep the handle.495kayan_get: proc<T>(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity) -> *T = {496    if (!kayan_alive(w, e)) {497        return null;498    }499    slot: *kayan_slot = vec<kayan_slot>at(w[0].slots&, cast(e.index, u64));500    t: *kayan_table = kayan_table_at(w, slot[0].table);501    if (!kayan_table_has(t, kayan_id_of<T>())) {502        return null;503    }504    rows: []T = kayan_slice<T>(t);505    return rows[cast(slot[0].row, u64)]&;506}507 508kayan_has: proc<T>(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity) -> b32 = {509    return (kayan_signature(w, e) & kayan_mask_of<T>()) != 0;510}511 512// Write e's T. It must already have one: giving an entity a component it does513// not have changes its table, which is 2.6.514kayan_set: proc<T>(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity, value: T) -> kayan_status = {515    if (!kayan_alive(w, e)) {516        return kayan_status.dead;517    }518    p: *T = kayan_get<T>(w, e);519    if (p == null) {520        return kayan_status.missing;521    }522    p[0] = value;523    return kayan_status.ok;524}525 526// Give e a T, or take its T away: the byte procs, with the type turned into an527// id and the value into its bytes.528kayan_add: proc<T>(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity, value: T) -> kayan_status = {529    bytes: [*]const u8 = cast(value&, [*]const u8);530    return kayan_add_id(w, e, kayan_id_of<T>(), bytes[0..sizeof(T)]);531}532 533kayan_remove: proc<T>(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity) -> kayan_status = {534    return kayan_remove_id(w, e, kayan_id_of<T>());535}536 537// The invariant, over every table: each row belongs to a live entity whose538// slot points back at that table and row, and the rows of all tables add up to539// the live count.540kayan_verify: proc(w: *kayan_world) -> u64 = {541    problems: u64 = 0;542    rows: u64 = 0;543    for (ti: u64 = 0; ti < w[0].tables.length; ti += 1) {544        t: *kayan_table = kayan_table_at(w, cast(ti, u32));545        for (row: u64 = 0; row < t[0].count; row += 1) {546            e: kayan_entity = t[0].entities[row];547            if (!kayan_alive(w, e)) {548                printfmt("kayan_verify: table {} row {} holds dead entity {}:{}\n", ti, row, e.index, e.generation);549                problems += 1;550                continue;551            }552            slot: *kayan_slot = vec<kayan_slot>at(w[0].slots&, cast(e.index, u64));553            if (cast(slot[0].table, u64) != ti || cast(slot[0].row, u64) != row) {554                printfmt("kayan_verify: {}:{} is in table {} row {}, its slot says table {} row {}\n",555                    e.index, e.generation, ti, row, slot[0].table, slot[0].row);556                problems += 1;557            }558        }559        rows += t[0].count;560    }561    if (rows != w[0].live) {562        printfmt("kayan_verify: {} rows in tables, {} live entities\n", rows, w[0].live);563        problems += 1;564    }565    return problems;566}567 568kayan_print_signature: proc(w: *kayan_world, signature: u64) -> void = {569    printf("{");570    first: b32 = true;571    for (id: u32 = 0; id < w[0].component_count; id += 1) {572        if ((signature & kayan_bit(id)) != 0) {573            printf(first ? "%s" : " %s", w[0].infos[id][0].name);574            first = false;575        }576    }577    printf("}");578}579 580kayan_print_table: proc(w: *kayan_world, ti: u32) -> void = {581    t: *kayan_table = kayan_table_at(w, ti);582    printf("    table %u ", ti);583    kayan_print_signature(w, t[0].signature);584    printf(":");585    for (row: u64 = 0; row < t[0].count; row += 1) {586        printf(" %u:%u", t[0].entities[row].index, t[0].entities[row].generation);587    }588    printf("\n");589}590 591kayan_print_tables: proc(w: *kayan_world) -> void = {592    for (ti: u32 = 0; ti < cast(w[0].tables.length, u32); ti += 1) {593        kayan_print_table(w, ti);594    }595}596 597// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------598// The inspector: reflect records, no component types599// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------600 601kayan_indent: proc(depth: u32) -> void = {602    for (i: u32 = 0; i < depth; i += 1) {603        printf("    ");604    }605}606 607// One value of a builtin type, read from its bytes by its type's name.608kayan_print_builtin: proc(type_name: [*]const char, at: []const u8) -> void = {609    if (strcmp(type_name, "f32") == 0) {610        printf("%.2f", cast(cast(at[0]&, *const f32)[0], f64));611    } else if (strcmp(type_name, "u32") == 0) {612        printf("%u", cast(at[0]&, *const u32)[0]);613    } else if (strcmp(type_name, "i32") == 0) {614        printf("%d", cast(at[0]&, *const i32)[0]);615    } else {616        printf("<%s>", type_name);617    }618}619 620// Every field of a struct whose bytes are `base`, nested structs indented621// under their field. A field's bytes are cut from `base` by its offset and622// size, both from the reflect record.623kayan_print_fields: proc(type: *const reflect, base: []const u8, depth: u32) -> void = {624    fields: [*]const reflect_field = reflect_fields(type);625    for (i: u64 = 0; i < type[0].count; i += 1) {626        f: *const reflect_field = fields[i]&;627        if (reflect_field_has_attr(f, "hidden")) {628            continue;629        }630        at: []const u8 = base[f[0].offset..f[0].offset + f[0].size];631        kayan_indent(depth);632        printf("%s:", f[0].name);633        info: *const reflect = f[0].info;634        if (info != null && info[0].kind == reflect_kind_struct) {635            printf("\n");636            kayan_print_fields(info, at, depth + 1);637        } else {638            printf(" ");639            kayan_print_builtin(f[0].type, at);640            printf("\n");641        }642    }643}644 645kayan_inspect: proc(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity) -> void = {646    if (!kayan_alive(w, e)) {647        printfmt("{}:{} (dead)\n", e.index, e.generation);648        return;649    }650    printf("%u:%u ", e.index, e.generation);651    signature: u64 = kayan_signature(w, e);652    kayan_print_signature(w, signature);653    printf("\n");654    for (id: u32 = 0; id < w[0].component_count; id += 1) {655        if ((signature & kayan_bit(id)) != 0) {656            info: *const reflect = w[0].infos[id];657            printf("    %s\n", info[0].name);658            bytes: []u8 = kayan_get_bytes(w, e, id);659            kayan_print_fields(info, bytes, 2);660        }661    }662}663 664// Every table: rows in use out of room, and per column its row size and its665// bytes in use out of bytes allocated. The memory a table holds and does not666// use is the cost of doubling on growth.667kayan_print_layout: proc(w: *kayan_world) -> void = {668    for (ti: u32 = 0; ti < cast(w[0].tables.length, u32); ti += 1) {669        t: *kayan_table = kayan_table_at(w, ti);670        printf("table %u ", ti);671        kayan_print_signature(w, t[0].signature);672        printf(": %u rows, room for %u\n", cast(t[0].count, u32), cast(t[0].capacity, u32));673        for (id: u32 = 0; id < w[0].component_count; id += 1) {674            if (kayan_table_has(t, id)) {675                size: u64 = t[0].columns[id].size;676                printf("    %-9s %2u bytes a row, %4u of %4u bytes in use\n", w[0].infos[id][0].name, cast(size, u32),677                    cast(size * t[0].count, u32), cast(size * t[0].capacity, u32));678            }679        }680    }681}682 683// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------684// Queries685// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------686 687// The tables a system runs over: every table whose signature has all of `all`688// and none of `none`, kept by index. Tables are only ever added, at the end of689// w.tables, so the query remembers how many it has checked and, brought up to690// date, looks at the new ones only.691kayan_query: struct = {692    all: u64;693    none: u64;694    tables: vec<u32>;695    checked: u64;696}697 698kayan_query_init: proc(all: u64, none: u64) -> kayan_query = {699    q: kayan_query = {};700    q.all = all;701    q.none = none;702    return q;703}704 705kayan_matches: proc(signature: u64, all: u64, none: u64) -> b32 = {706    return (signature & all) == all && (signature & none) == 0;707}708 709// Check the tables made since the query last looked. With none new, this is710// one comparison, so call it before every walk.711kayan_query_update: proc(w: *kayan_world, q: *kayan_query) -> void = {712    for (ti: u64 = q[0].checked; ti < w[0].tables.length; ti += 1) {713        if (kayan_matches(kayan_table_at(w, cast(ti, u32))[0].signature, q[0].all, q[0].none)) {714            _ = vec<u32>append(w[0].arena, q[0].tables&, cast(ti, u32));715        }716    }717    q[0].checked = w[0].tables.length;718}719 720// The query's i-th table. Like any table pointer, good until a table is made.721kayan_query_table: proc(w: *kayan_world, q: *kayan_query, i: u64) -> *kayan_table = {722    return kayan_table_at(w, vec<u32>at(q[0].tables&, i)[0]);723}724 725// How many entities the query matches: the rows of its tables.726kayan_query_count: proc(w: *kayan_world, q: *kayan_query) -> u64 = {727    kayan_query_update(w, q);728    n: u64 = 0;729    for (i: u64 = 0; i < q[0].tables.length; i += 1) {730        n += kayan_query_table(w, q, i)[0].count;731    }732    return n;733}734 735kayan_print_query: proc(w: *kayan_world, name: [*]const char, q: *kayan_query) -> void = {736    kayan_query_update(w, q);737    printf("%s: all ", name);738    kayan_print_signature(w, q[0].all);739    printf(", none ");740    kayan_print_signature(w, q[0].none);741    printfmt("; tables: {}, entities: {}\n", q[0].tables.length, kayan_query_count(w, q));742    for (i: u64 = 0; i < q[0].tables.length; i += 1) {743        kayan_print_table(w, vec<u32>at(q[0].tables&, i)[0]);744    }745}746 747// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------748// Commands749// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------750 751// A spawn that has been recorded and not applied. There is no entity yet, so752// this is the spawn command's place in the list; give it components with753// kayan_pending_set.754kayan_pending: struct = {755    command: u32;756}757 758kayan_defer: proc(w: *kayan_world, c: kayan_command) -> u32 = {759    index: u32 = cast(w[0].commands.length, u32);760    _ = vec<kayan_command>append(w[0].frame&, w[0].commands&, c);761    return index;762}763 764// A copy of `value`, as bytes, in the frame arena.765kayan_defer_value: proc<T>(w: *kayan_world, value: T) -> []u8 = {766    data: [*]u8 = cast(memops_arena_push(w[0].frame&, sizeof(T), alignof(T)), [*]u8);767    memcpy(data[0]&, value&, sizeof(T));768    return data[0..sizeof(T)];769}770 771kayan_defer_spawn: proc(w: *kayan_world, signature: u64) -> kayan_pending = {772    p: kayan_pending = {};773    p.command = kayan_defer(w, { .kind = kayan_command_kind.spawn, .signature = signature });774    return p;775}776 777kayan_pending_set: proc<T>(w: *kayan_world, p: kayan_pending, value: T) -> void = {778    _ = kayan_defer(w, { .kind = kayan_command_kind.add, .spawn = p.command + 1, .id = kayan_id_of<T>(),779        .value = kayan_defer_value<T>(w, value) });780}781 782kayan_defer_despawn: proc(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity) -> void = {783    _ = kayan_defer(w, { .kind = kayan_command_kind.despawn, .entity = e });784}785 786kayan_defer_add: proc<T>(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity, value: T) -> void = {787    _ = kayan_defer(w, { .kind = kayan_command_kind.add, .entity = e, .id = kayan_id_of<T>(),788        .value = kayan_defer_value<T>(w, value) });789}790 791kayan_defer_remove: proc<T>(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity) -> void = {792    _ = kayan_defer(w, { .kind = kayan_command_kind.remove, .entity = e, .id = kayan_id_of<T>() });793}794 795// One applied command. The components given to a new entity are part of its796// spawn line, so they are not printed on their own.797kayan_print_command: proc(w: *kayan_world, c: *kayan_command, status: kayan_status) -> void = {798    if (c[0].spawn != 0 && status == kayan_status.ok) {799        return;800    }801    printfmt("    {} ", c[0].kind);802    if (c[0].kind == kayan_command_kind.spawn) {803        kayan_print_signature(w, c[0].signature);804        printf(" -> ");805    } else if (c[0].kind != kayan_command_kind.despawn) {806        printf("%s, ", w[0].infos[c[0].id][0].name);807    }808    printf("%u:%u", c[0].entity.index, c[0].entity.generation);809    if (status != kayan_status.ok) {810        printfmt(": skipped, {}", status);811    }812    printf("\n");813}814 815// Apply the frame's commands in the order they were recorded, then let them816// all go at once. A command for an entity that died after it was recorded817// (despawned by an earlier command, most likely) does nothing, and is counted.818kayan_flush: proc(w: *kayan_world) -> void = {819    for (i: u64 = 0; i < w[0].commands.length; i += 1) {820        c: *kayan_command = vec<kayan_command>at(w[0].commands&, i);821        if (c[0].spawn != 0) {822            c[0].entity = vec<kayan_command>at(w[0].commands&, cast(c[0].spawn - 1, u64))[0].entity;823        }824        status: kayan_status = kayan_status.ok;825        if (c[0].kind == kayan_command_kind.spawn) {826            c[0].entity = kayan_spawn(w, c[0].signature);827        } else if (c[0].kind == kayan_command_kind.despawn) {828            status = kayan_despawn(w, c[0].entity);829        } else if (c[0].kind == kayan_command_kind.add) {830            status = kayan_add_id(w, c[0].entity, c[0].id, c[0].value);831        } else {832            status = kayan_remove_id(w, c[0].entity, c[0].id);833        }834        if (status == kayan_status.ok) {835            w[0].applied += 1;836        } else {837            w[0].skipped += 1;838        }839        if (w[0].trace) {840            kayan_print_command(w, c, status);841        }842    }843    w[0].commands = {};844    memops_arena_clear(w[0].frame&);845}846 847// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------848// Systems849// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------850 851// What a system gets for each table it runs on: the world, the table, and the852// frame's time step. One struct rather than three parameters, so that adding853// to it later changes no system's signature.854kayan_iter: struct = {855    world: *kayan_world;856    table: *kayan_table;857    dt: f32;858    ctx: *void;859}860 861kayan_system_proc: alias = *proc(it: *kayan_iter) -> void;862 863// A system: a name, the query that finds its tables, and the proc run on each864// of those tables that has rows. `tables` and `rows` count what it has run865// over. `ctx` is handed to the proc as is: whatever the system needs beyond866// its own tables, such as another query, or the game's state.867kayan_system: struct = {868    name: [*]const char;869    query: kayan_query;870    run: kayan_system_proc;871    ctx: *void;872    tables: u64;873    rows: u64;874}875 876kayan_system_init: proc(name: [*]const char, all: u64, none: u64, run: kayan_system_proc, ctx: *void) -> kayan_system = {877    s: kayan_system = {};878    s.name = name;879    s.query = kayan_query_init(all, none);880    s.run = run;881    s.ctx = ctx;882    return s;883}884 885// One frame: every system in order, each over every table it matches that has886// rows, then the commands they recorded. A system sees every value the887// systems before it wrote this frame, and no structural change until the888// next.889kayan_progress: proc(w: *kayan_world, systems: []kayan_system, dt: f32) -> void = {890    for (s: u64 = 0; s < systems.length; s += 1) {891        sys: *kayan_system = systems[s]&;892        kayan_query_update(w, sys[0].query&);893        for (i: u64 = 0; i < sys[0].query.tables.length; i += 1) {894            it: kayan_iter = {};895            it.world = w;896            it.table = kayan_query_table(w, sys[0].query&, i);897            it.dt = dt;898            it.ctx = sys[0].ctx;899            if (it.table[0].count > 0) {900                sys[0].tables += 1;901                sys[0].rows += it.table[0].count;902                sys[0].run(it&);903            }904        }905    }906    kayan_flush(w);907}908 909kayan_print_schedule: proc(w: *kayan_world, systems: []kayan_system) -> void = {910    for (s: u64 = 0; s < systems.length; s += 1) {911        kayan_print_query(w, systems[s].name, systems[s].query&);912    }913}914 915// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------916// The program917// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------918 919bullet_signature: proc() -> u64 = {920    return kayan_mask_of<position>() | kayan_mask_of<velocity>() | kayan_mask_of<damage>() | kayan_mask_of<lifetime>();921}922 923spawn_bullet: proc(w: *kayan_world, x: f32, seconds: f32) -> kayan_entity = {924    e: kayan_entity = kayan_spawn(w, bullet_signature());925    _ = kayan_set<position>(w, e, { .at = { .x = x, .y = 0.0 } });926    _ = kayan_set<velocity>(w, e, { .per_second = { .x = 8.0, .y = 0.0 } });927    _ = kayan_set<damage>(w, e, { .amount = 25.0 });928    _ = kayan_set<lifetime>(w, e, { .seconds = seconds });929    return e;930}931 932spawn_target: proc(w: *kayan_world, x: f32, y: f32) -> kayan_entity = {933    e: kayan_entity = kayan_spawn(w, kayan_mask_of<position>() | kayan_mask_of<health>());934    _ = kayan_set<position>(w, e, { .at = { .x = x, .y = y } });935    _ = kayan_set<health>(w, e, { .points = 100.0, .max = 100.0 });936    return e;937}938 939// The wrong way: despawn as the loop goes. The table does not change until the952// frame is over, so every row is looked at once.953expire_system: proc(it: *kayan_iter) -> void = {954    ls: []lifetime = kayan_slice<lifetime>(it[0].table);955    es: []kayan_entity = kayan_entities(it[0].table);956    for (row: u64 = 0; row < es.length; row += 1) {957        if (ls[row].seconds <= 0.0) {958            kayan_defer_despawn(it[0].world, es[row]);959        }960    }961}962 963age_system: proc(it: *kayan_iter) -> void = {964    ls: []lifetime = kayan_slice<lifetime>(it[0].table);965    for (row: u64 = 0; row < ls.length; row += 1) {966        ls[row].seconds -= it[0].dt;967    }968}969 970move_system: proc(it: *kayan_iter) -> void = {971    ps: []position = kayan_slice<position>(it[0].table);972    vs: []velocity = kayan_slice<velocity>(it[0].table);973    for (row: u64 = 0; row < ps.length; row += 1) {974        ps[row].at.x += vs[row].per_second.x * it[0].dt;975        ps[row].at.y += vs[row].per_second.y * it[0].dt;976    }977}978 979// A turret whose timer is up spawns a bullet where it stands. The bullet does980// not exist until the frame ends, so it first moves next frame.981turret_system: proc(it: *kayan_iter) -> void = {982    ps: []position = kayan_slice<position>(it[0].table);983    ts: []turret = kayan_slice<turret>(it[0].table);984    for (row: u64 = 0; row < ts.length; row += 1) {985        if (ts[row].timer <= 0.0) {986            shot: kayan_pending = kayan_defer_spawn(it[0].world, bullet_signature());987            kayan_pending_set<position>(it[0].world, shot, ps[row]);988            kayan_pending_set<velocity>(it[0].world, shot, { .per_second = { .x = 8.0, .y = 0.0 } });989            kayan_pending_set<damage>(it[0].world, shot, { .amount = 25.0 });990            kayan_pending_set<lifetime>(it[0].world, shot, { .seconds = 2.0 });991            ts[row].timer += ts[row].cooldown;992        }993        ts[row].timer -= it[0].dt;994    }995}996 997// A bullet within half a unit of a target hits it. During a1000// frame no table is made or moved, so walking a second query is safe.1001hit_system: proc(it: *kayan_iter) -> void = {1002    w: *kayan_world = it[0].world;1003    targets: *kayan_query = cast(it[0].ctx, *kayan_query);1004    ps: []position = kayan_slice<position>(it[0].table);1005    ds: []damage = kayan_slice<damage>(it[0].table);1006    es: []kayan_entity = kayan_entities(it[0].table);1007    kayan_query_update(w, targets);1008    for (b: u64 = 0; b < es.length; b += 1) {1009        for (i: u64 = 0; i < targets[0].tables.length; i += 1) {1010            t: *kayan_table = kayan_query_table(w, targets, i);1011            tps: []position = kayan_slice<position>(t);1012            ths: []health = kayan_slice<health>(t);1013            for (row: u64 = 0; row < tps.length; row += 1) {1014                dx: f32 = tps[row].at.x - ps[b].at.x;1015                dy: f32 = tps[row].at.y - ps[b].at.y;1016                if (dx * dx + dy * dy < 0.25) {1017                    ths[row].points -= ds[b].amount;1018                    kayan_defer_despawn(w, es[b]);1019                }1020            }1021        }1022    }1023}1024 1025make_world: proc(w: *kayan_world, arena: *memops_arena) -> void = {1026    kayan_world_init(w, arena);1027    kayan_register(w, kayan_id_of<position>(), position<>&);1028    kayan_register(w, kayan_id_of<velocity>(), velocity<>&);1029    kayan_register(w, kayan_id_of<health>(), health<>&);1030    kayan_register(w, kayan_id_of<damage>(), damage<>&);1031    kayan_register(w, kayan_id_of<lifetime>(), lifetime<>&);1032    kayan_register(w, kayan_id_of<turret>(), turret<>&);1033    kayan_register(w, kayan_id_of<burning>(), burning<>&);1034}1035 1036// Four bullets, three of them out of time.1037four_bullets: proc(w: *kayan_world) -> void = {1038    _ = spawn_bullet(w, 1.0, 0.0);1039    _ = spawn_bullet(w, 2.0, 1.0);1040    _ = spawn_bullet(w, 3.0, 0.0);1041    _ = spawn_bullet(w, 4.0, 0.0);1042}1043 1044print_lifetimes: proc(w: *kayan_world) -> void = {1045    t: *kayan_table = kayan_table_at(w, kayan_table_for(w, bullet_signature()));1046    ls: []lifetime = kayan_slice<lifetime>(t);1047    printf("    lifetimes:");1048    for (row: u64 = 0; row < t[0].count; row += 1) {1049        printf("  %u:%u %.2f", t[0].entities[row].index, t[0].entities[row].generation, cast(ls[row].seconds, f64));1050    }1051    printf("\n");1052}1053 1054main: proc() -> i32 = {1055    arena: memops_arena = {};1056    memops_arena_initialize(arena&);1057    lifetime_only: u64 = kayan_mask_of<lifetime>();1058 1059    printfmt("1. an expire system that despawns as it goes\n");1060    a: kayan_world = {};1061    make_world(a&, arena&);1062    four_bullets(a&);1063    print_lifetimes(a&);1064    wrong: [1]kayan_system = {};1065    wrong[0] = kayan_system_init("expire", lifetime_only, 0, expire_now_system, null);1066    kayan_progress(a&, wrong, 0.25);1067    printfmt("after one frame:\n");1068    print_lifetimes(a&);1069    printfmt("kayan_verify: {} problems. Build an ECS · part 3, systems · 3.4

A game

ecs/src/3.systems/3.4.game/game.rin

Everything together. Three lanes, a turret at the left end of each, and drones coming from the right in waves:

  • a turret fires down its lane while there's a drone in it;
  • a bullet that reaches a drone damages it;
  • a drone below half health catches fire;
  • a drone with no health left is destroyed;
  • a drone that gets to the left end has reached the base.

The top of the file is kayan, exactly as 3.3 left it. The game is the bottom: components, kernels, systems, a schedule and a level script. Every rule of the game is a system over a query. Every structural change a system makes is a command.

The pieces

The components are the same seven from 2.1. A drone is a signature:

drone_signature: proc() -> u64 = {
    return kayan_mask_of<position>() | kayan_mask_of<velocity>() | kayan_mask_of<health>();
}

A burning drone is that plus burning, which puts it in another table. There is no drone type anywhere in the program. A drone is whatever lives in a table with these columns.

What the systems share (the drones query, the clock, the score) is one struct, handed to the systems that need it through ctx:

game: struct = {
    drones: kayan_query;
    time: f32;
    fired: u32;
    hits: u32;
    fires: u32;
    kills: u32;
    breaches: u32;
    came: u32;
}

The schedule

    systems: [9]kayan_system = {};
    systems[0] = kayan_system_init("turret", shooting, 0, turret_system, g&);
    systems[1] = kayan_system_init("age", kayan_mask_of<lifetime>(), 0, age_system, null);
    systems[2] = kayan_system_init("expire", kayan_mask_of<lifetime>(), 0, expire_system, null);
    systems[3] = kayan_system_init("move", movers, 0, move_system, null);
    systems[4] = kayan_system_init("hit", bullets, 0, hit_system, g&);
    systems[5] = kayan_system_init("ignite", kayan_mask_of<health>(), kayan_mask_of<burning>(), ignite_system, g&);
    systems[6] = kayan_system_init("burn", kayan_mask_of<health>() | kayan_mask_of<burning>(), 0, burn_system, null);
    systems[7] = kayan_system_init("die", kayan_mask_of<health>(), 0, die_system, g&);
    systems[8] = kayan_system_init("breach", kayan_mask_of<position>() | kayan_mask_of<health>(), 0, breach_system, g&);

Read it as the frame, top to bottom. Each line's position is a data-flow decision (3.2):

  • move before hit: bullets hit where they are, not where they were.
  • hit before ignite, burn and die: a drone takes damage, catches fire and is destroyed in the same frame its health drops.
  • die before breach: only a drone that survived the frame can reach the base. breach also checks health > 0 itself, because both run in the same frame and die's despawn hasn't been applied yet.
  • ignite has none {burning}: a drone catches fire once. The add is a command, so next frame it's in the burning table and the query no longer matches it.

The rules

Each one is a few lines. The ones that only change values call kernels:

burn_system: proc(it: *kayan_iter) -> void = {
    burn(kayan_slice<health>(it[0].table), kayan_slice<burning>(it[0].table), it[0].dt);
}

The ones that change structure record commands:

        if (hs[row].points < 0.5 * hs[row].max && hs[row].points > 0.0) {
            kayan_defer_add<burning>(it[0].world, es[row], { .per_second = 10.0 });
            g[0].fires += 1;
        }

The turret is the most involved. It asks the drones query whether anything is ahead of it in its lane, then spawns a bullet with a pending spawn (3.3):

        if (ts[row].timer <= 0.0 && drone_ahead(it[0].world, g, ps[row].at.x, ps[row].at.y)) {

hit is 3.3's hit system, with one extra thought about speed. A bullet moves a unit a frame and a fast drone a quarter, so they close by at most 1.25 a frame. A hit window of ±0.75 is 1.5 wide, so no bullet can pass through a drone between two frames:

                if (dx * dx < 0.5625 && dy * dy < 0.25) {

The level

The waves aren't a system. They're the level script, and it runs between frames, in the game loop, where spawning directly is safe:

    for (frame: u32 = 0; frame < frames; frame += 1) {
        g.time = cast(frame, f32) * dt;
        if (frame % 32 == 0 && frame / 32 < 8) {
            send_wave(w&, g&, frame / 32);
        }
        kayan_progress(w&, systems, dt);
        problems += kayan_verify(w&);

kayan_verify runs after every frame: 512 checks of Part 1's invariant over the whole world.

Drawing by table

The picture of the lanes walks a query of everything with a position. What an entity is drawn as comes from its table's signature, decided once per table, not per entity:

glyph_of: proc(signature: u64) -> i32 = {
    if ((signature & kayan_mask_of<turret>()) != 0) {
        return 'T';
    }
    if ((signature & kayan_mask_of<burning>()) != 0) {
        return '*';
    }
    if ((signature & kayan_mask_of<health>()) != 0) {
        return 'd';
    }
    return '-';
}

In an OOP engine this would be a virtual draw() per object. Here it's a property of a table, and the inner loop is a plain loop over positions.

Exact on purpose

Every speed and time step is a power of two: dt is 1/16, drones move 2 or 4 units a second, bullets 16, fire burns 10 a second (0.625 a frame). So every position, health and timer is exactly representable, and no rounding ever happens. That's why a Debug build, a Release build, gcc, clang and a CPU that fuses multiply-adds all print the same game. Real games give that up for nicer numbers. Rounding differences usually don't matter, but they do the day you want a replay or a lockstep network game.

What you built

Part 1  entities       handles, generations, slots, swap-remove, kayan_verify
Part 2  components     ids, columns, tables, archetypes, typed access,
                       moving between tables, the archetype graph, reflection
Part 3  systems        queries, kernels and schedules, commands, a game

That's a working archetype ECS, about 650 lines of kayan without comments. It's the design flecs is built on (tables, the archetype graph, cached queries, command buffers), and Bevy and Unity DOTS are close cousins, minus their years of features.

Things worth adding next, roughly in order of how much they teach:

  • Relationships: child_of(parent) as a component, flecs' big idea.
  • Change detection: a per-column version number, so a system can skip tables nothing wrote to.
  • Parallel systems: systems that don't write what others read can run at the same time. The schedule already holds what you need to decide that.
  • Removing empty tables, and the queries' table lists with them.
  • Serialization: the reflect records already describe every byte; write the tables out and read them back.

Try

  1. Add a fourth lane. What changes? (Only the level: lanes, the picture.)
  2. Make bullets pierce: they don't despawn on a hit, but each drone can only be hit by a bullet once. Where does "once" live? (A component on the bullet? On the drone?)
  3. Add a shield component that absorbs the next hit, then removes itself. Which systems change?
  4. Print kayan_inspect of a drone the frame it catches fire.

Handle, slot, table, row, typed494// view: the same path as 1.4's get_position, for any component. The pointer is495// good until the next structural change, so use it now and keep the handle.496kayan_get: proc<T>(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity) -> *T = {497    if (!kayan_alive(w, e)) {498        return null;499    }500    slot: *kayan_slot = vec<kayan_slot>at(w[0].slots&, cast(e.index, u64));501    t: *kayan_table = kayan_table_at(w, slot[0].table);502    if (!kayan_table_has(t, kayan_id_of<T>())) {503        return null;504    }505    rows: []T = kayan_slice<T>(t);506    return rows[cast(slot[0].row, u64)]&;507}508 509kayan_has: proc<T>(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity) -> b32 = {510    return (kayan_signature(w, e) & kayan_mask_of<T>()) != 0;511}512 513// Write e's T. It must already have one: giving an entity a component it does514// not have changes its table, which is 2.6.515kayan_set: proc<T>(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity, value: T) -> kayan_status = {516    if (!kayan_alive(w, e)) {517        return kayan_status.dead;518    }519    p: *T = kayan_get<T>(w, e);520    if (p == null) {521        return kayan_status.missing;522    }523    p[0] = value;524    return kayan_status.ok;525}526 527// Give e a T, or take its T away: the byte procs, with the type turned into an528// id and the value into its bytes.529kayan_add: proc<T>(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity, value: T) -> kayan_status = {530    bytes: [*]const u8 = cast(value&, [*]const u8);531    return kayan_add_id(w, e, kayan_id_of<T>(), bytes[0..sizeof(T)]);532}533 534kayan_remove: proc<T>(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity) -> kayan_status = {535    return kayan_remove_id(w, e, kayan_id_of<T>());536}537 538// The invariant, over every table: each row belongs to a live entity whose539// slot points back at that table and row, and the rows of all tables add up to540// the live count.541kayan_verify: proc(w: *kayan_world) -> u64 = {542    problems: u64 = 0;543    rows: u64 = 0;544    for (ti: u64 = 0; ti < w[0].tables.length; ti += 1) {545        t: *kayan_table = kayan_table_at(w, cast(ti, u32));546        for (row: u64 = 0; row < t[0].count; row += 1) {547            e: kayan_entity = t[0].entities[row];548            if (!kayan_alive(w, e)) {549                printfmt("kayan_verify: table {} row {} holds dead entity {}:{}\n", ti, row, e.index, e.generation);550                problems += 1;551                continue;552            }553            slot: *kayan_slot = vec<kayan_slot>at(w[0].slots&, cast(e.index, u64));554            if (cast(slot[0].table, u64) != ti || cast(slot[0].row, u64) != row) {555                printfmt("kayan_verify: {}:{} is in table {} row {}, its slot says table {} row {}\n",556                    e.index, e.generation, ti, row, slot[0].table, slot[0].row);557                problems += 1;558            }559        }560        rows += t[0].count;561    }562    if (rows != w[0].live) {563        printfmt("kayan_verify: {} rows in tables, {} live entities\n", rows, w[0].live);564        problems += 1;565    }566    return problems;567}568 569kayan_print_signature: proc(w: *kayan_world, signature: u64) -> void = {570    printf("{");571    first: b32 = true;572    for (id: u32 = 0; id < w[0].component_count; id += 1) {573        if ((signature & kayan_bit(id)) != 0) {574            printf(first ? "%s" : " %s", w[0].infos[id][0].name);575            first = false;576        }577    }578    printf("}");579}580 581kayan_print_table: proc(w: *kayan_world, ti: u32) -> void = {582    t: *kayan_table = kayan_table_at(w, ti);583    printf("    table %u ", ti);584    kayan_print_signature(w, t[0].signature);585    printf(":");586    for (row: u64 = 0; row < t[0].count; row += 1) {587        printf(" %u:%u", t[0].entities[row].index, t[0].entities[row].generation);588    }589    printf("\n");590}591 592kayan_print_tables: proc(w: *kayan_world) -> void = {593    for (ti: u32 = 0; ti < cast(w[0].tables.length, u32); ti += 1) {594        kayan_print_table(w, ti);595    }596}597 598// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------599// The inspector: reflect records, no component types600// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------601 602kayan_indent: proc(depth: u32) -> void = {603    for (i: u32 = 0; i < depth; i += 1) {604        printf("    ");605    }606}607 608// One value of a builtin type, read from its bytes by its type's name.609kayan_print_builtin: proc(type_name: [*]const char, at: []const u8) -> void = {610    if (strcmp(type_name, "f32") == 0) {611        printf("%.2f", cast(cast(at[0]&, *const f32)[0], f64));612    } else if (strcmp(type_name, "u32") == 0) {613        printf("%u", cast(at[0]&, *const u32)[0]);614    } else if (strcmp(type_name, "i32") == 0) {615        printf("%d", cast(at[0]&, *const i32)[0]);616    } else {617        printf("<%s>", type_name);618    }619}620 621// Every field of a struct whose bytes are `base`, nested structs indented622// under their field. A field's bytes are cut from `base` by its offset and623// size, both from the reflect record.624kayan_print_fields: proc(type: *const reflect, base: []const u8, depth: u32) -> void = {625    fields: [*]const reflect_field = reflect_fields(type);626    for (i: u64 = 0; i < type[0].count; i += 1) {627        f: *const reflect_field = fields[i]&;628        if (reflect_field_has_attr(f, "hidden")) {629            continue;630        }631        at: []const u8 = base[f[0].offset..f[0].offset + f[0].size];632        kayan_indent(depth);633        printf("%s:", f[0].name);634        info: *const reflect = f[0].info;635        if (info != null && info[0].kind == reflect_kind_struct) {636            printf("\n");637            kayan_print_fields(info, at, depth + 1);638        } else {639            printf(" ");640            kayan_print_builtin(f[0].type, at);641            printf("\n");642        }643    }644}645 646kayan_inspect: proc(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity) -> void = {647    if (!kayan_alive(w, e)) {648        printfmt("{}:{} (dead)\n", e.index, e.generation);649        return;650    }651    printf("%u:%u ", e.index, e.generation);652    signature: u64 = kayan_signature(w, e);653    kayan_print_signature(w, signature);654    printf("\n");655    for (id: u32 = 0; id < w[0].component_count; id += 1) {656        if ((signature & kayan_bit(id)) != 0) {657            info: *const reflect = w[0].infos[id];658            printf("    %s\n", info[0].name);659            bytes: []u8 = kayan_get_bytes(w, e, id);660            kayan_print_fields(info, bytes, 2);661        }662    }663}664 665// Every table: rows in use out of room, and per column its row size and its666// bytes in use out of bytes allocated. The memory a table holds and does not667// use is the cost of doubling on growth.668kayan_print_layout: proc(w: *kayan_world) -> void = {669    for (ti: u32 = 0; ti < cast(w[0].tables.length, u32); ti += 1) {670        t: *kayan_table = kayan_table_at(w, ti);671        printf("table %u ", ti);672        kayan_print_signature(w, t[0].signature);673        printf(": %u rows, room for %u\n", cast(t[0].count, u32), cast(t[0].capacity, u32));674        for (id: u32 = 0; id < w[0].component_count; id += 1) {675            if (kayan_table_has(t, id)) {676                size: u64 = t[0].columns[id].size;677                printf("    %-9s %2u bytes a row, %4u of %4u bytes in use\n", w[0].infos[id][0].name, cast(size, u32),678                    cast(size * t[0].count, u32), cast(size * t[0].capacity, u32));679            }680        }681    }682}683 684// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------685// Queries686// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------687 688// The tables a system runs over: every table whose signature has all of `all`689// and none of `none`, kept by index. Tables are only ever added, at the end of690// w.tables, so the query remembers how many it has checked and, brought up to691// date, looks at the new ones only.692kayan_query: struct = {693    all: u64;694    none: u64;695    tables: vec<u32>;696    checked: u64;697}698 699kayan_query_init: proc(all: u64, none: u64) -> kayan_query = {700    q: kayan_query = {};701    q.all = all;702    q.none = none;703    return q;704}705 706kayan_matches: proc(signature: u64, all: u64, none: u64) -> b32 = {707    return (signature & all) == all && (signature & none) == 0;708}709 710// Check the tables made since the query last looked. With none new, this is711// one comparison, so call it before every walk.712kayan_query_update: proc(w: *kayan_world, q: *kayan_query) -> void = {713    for (ti: u64 = q[0].checked; ti < w[0].tables.length; ti += 1) {714        if (kayan_matches(kayan_table_at(w, cast(ti, u32))[0].signature, q[0].all, q[0].none)) {715            _ = vec<u32>append(w[0].arena, q[0].tables&, cast(ti, u32));716        }717    }718    q[0].checked = w[0].tables.length;719}720 721// The query's i-th table. Like any table pointer, good until a table is made.722kayan_query_table: proc(w: *kayan_world, q: *kayan_query, i: u64) -> *kayan_table = {723    return kayan_table_at(w, vec<u32>at(q[0].tables&, i)[0]);724}725 726// How many entities the query matches: the rows of its tables.727kayan_query_count: proc(w: *kayan_world, q: *kayan_query) -> u64 = {728    kayan_query_update(w, q);729    n: u64 = 0;730    for (i: u64 = 0; i < q[0].tables.length; i += 1) {731        n += kayan_query_table(w, q, i)[0].count;732    }733    return n;734}735 736kayan_print_query: proc(w: *kayan_world, name: [*]const char, q: *kayan_query) -> void = {737    kayan_query_update(w, q);738    printf("%s: all ", name);739    kayan_print_signature(w, q[0].all);740    printf(", none ");741    kayan_print_signature(w, q[0].none);742    printfmt("; tables: {}, entities: {}\n", q[0].tables.length, kayan_query_count(w, q));743    for (i: u64 = 0; i < q[0].tables.length; i += 1) {744        kayan_print_table(w, vec<u32>at(q[0].tables&, i)[0]);745    }746}747 748// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------749// Commands750// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------751 752// A spawn that has been recorded and not applied. There is no entity yet, so753// this is the spawn command's place in the list; give it components with754// kayan_pending_set.755kayan_pending: struct = {756    command: u32;757}758 759kayan_defer: proc(w: *kayan_world, c: kayan_command) -> u32 = {760    index: u32 = cast(w[0].commands.length, u32);761    _ = vec<kayan_command>append(w[0].frame&, w[0].commands&, c);762    return index;763}764 765// A copy of `value`, as bytes, in the frame arena.766kayan_defer_value: proc<T>(w: *kayan_world, value: T) -> []u8 = {767    data: [*]u8 = cast(memops_arena_push(w[0].frame&, sizeof(T), alignof(T)), [*]u8);768    memcpy(data[0]&, value&, sizeof(T));769    return data[0..sizeof(T)];770}771 772kayan_defer_spawn: proc(w: *kayan_world, signature: u64) -> kayan_pending = {773    p: kayan_pending = {};774    p.command = kayan_defer(w, { .kind = kayan_command_kind.spawn, .signature = signature });775    return p;776}777 778kayan_pending_set: proc<T>(w: *kayan_world, p: kayan_pending, value: T) -> void = {779    _ = kayan_defer(w, { .kind = kayan_command_kind.add, .spawn = p.command + 1, .id = kayan_id_of<T>(),780        .value = kayan_defer_value<T>(w, value) });781}782 783kayan_defer_despawn: proc(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity) -> void = {784    _ = kayan_defer(w, { .kind = kayan_command_kind.despawn, .entity = e });785}786 787kayan_defer_add: proc<T>(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity, value: T) -> void = {788    _ = kayan_defer(w, { .kind = kayan_command_kind.add, .entity = e, .id = kayan_id_of<T>(),789        .value = kayan_defer_value<T>(w, value) });790}791 792kayan_defer_remove: proc<T>(w: *kayan_world, e: kayan_entity) -> void = {793    _ = kayan_defer(w, { .kind = kayan_command_kind.remove, .entity = e, .id = kayan_id_of<T>() });794}795 796// One applied command. The components given to a new entity are part of its797// spawn line, so they are not printed on their own.798kayan_print_command: proc(w: *kayan_world, c: *kayan_command, status: kayan_status) -> void = {799    if (c[0].spawn != 0 && status == kayan_status.ok) {800        return;801    }802    printfmt("    {} ", c[0].kind);803    if (c[0].kind == kayan_command_kind.spawn) {804        kayan_print_signature(w, c[0].signature);805        printf(" -> ");806    } else if (c[0].kind != kayan_command_kind.despawn) {807        printf("%s, ", w[0].infos[c[0].id][0].name);808    }809    printf("%u:%u", c[0].entity.index, c[0].entity.generation);810    if (status != kayan_status.ok) {811        printfmt(": skipped, {}", status);812    }813    printf("\n");814}815 816// Apply the frame's commands in the order they were recorded, then let them817// all go at once. A command for an entity that died after it was recorded818// (despawned by an earlier command, most likely) does nothing, and is counted.819kayan_flush: proc(w: *kayan_world) -> void = {820    for (i: u64 = 0; i < w[0].commands.length; i += 1) {821        c: *kayan_command = vec<kayan_command>at(w[0].commands&, i);822        if (c[0].spawn != 0) {823            c[0].entity = vec<kayan_command>at(w[0].commands&, cast(c[0].spawn - 1, u64))[0].entity;824        }825        status: kayan_status = kayan_status.ok;826        if (c[0].kind == kayan_command_kind.spawn) {827            c[0].entity = kayan_spawn(w, c[0].signature);828        } else if (c[0].kind == kayan_command_kind.despawn) {829            status = kayan_despawn(w, c[0].entity);830        } else if (c[0].kind == kayan_command_kind.add) {831            status = kayan_add_id(w, c[0].entity, c[0].id, c[0].value);832        } else {833            status = kayan_remove_id(w, c[0].entity, c[0].id);834        }835        if (status == kayan_status.ok) {836            w[0].applied += 1;837        } else {838            w[0].skipped += 1;839        }840        if (w[0].trace) {841            kayan_print_command(w, c, status);842        }843    }844    w[0].commands = {};845    memops_arena_clear(w[0].frame&);846}847 848// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------849// Systems850// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------851 852// What a system gets for each table it runs on: the world, the table, and the853// frame's time step. One struct rather than three parameters, so that adding854// to it later changes no system's signature.855kayan_iter: struct = {856    world: *kayan_world;857    table: *kayan_table;858    dt: f32;859    ctx: *void;860}861 862kayan_system_proc: alias = *proc(it: *kayan_iter) -> void;863 864// A system: a name, the query that finds its tables, and the proc run on each865// of those tables that has rows. `tables` and `rows` count what it has run866// over. `ctx` is handed to the proc as is: whatever the system needs beyond867// its own tables, such as another query, or the game's state.868kayan_system: struct = {869    name: [*]const char;870    query: kayan_query;871    run: kayan_system_proc;872    ctx: *void;873    tables: u64;874    rows: u64;875}876 877kayan_system_init: proc(name: [*]const char, all: u64, none: u64, run: kayan_system_proc, ctx: *void) -> kayan_system = {878    s: kayan_system = {};879    s.name = name;880    s.query = kayan_query_init(all, none);881    s.run = run;882    s.ctx = ctx;883    return s;884}885 886// One frame: every system in order, each over every table it matches that has887// rows, then the commands they recorded. A system sees every value the888// systems before it wrote this frame, and no structural change until the889// next.890kayan_progress: proc(w: *kayan_world, systems: []kayan_system, dt: f32) -> void = {891    for (s: u64 = 0; s < systems.length; s += 1) {892        sys: *kayan_system = systems[s]&;893        kayan_query_update(w, sys[0].query&);894        for (i: u64 = 0; i < sys[0].query.tables.length; i += 1) {895            it: kayan_iter = {};896            it.world = w;897            it.table = kayan_query_table(w, sys[0].query&, i);898            it.dt = dt;899            it.ctx = sys[0].ctx;900            if (it.table[0].count > 0) {901                sys[0].tables += 1;902                sys[0].rows += it.table[0].count;903                sys[0].run(it&);904            }905        }906    }907    kayan_flush(w);908}909 910kayan_print_schedule: proc(w: *kayan_world, systems: []kayan_system) -> void = {911    for (s: u64 = 0; s < systems.length; s += 1) {912        kayan_print_query(w, systems[s].name, systems[s].query&);913    }914}915 916// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------917// The program918// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------919 920// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------921// The game922// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------923 924// What the game's systems share: the drones, for the systems that look for925// them, and the score. Systems get it through their ctx.926game: struct = {927    drones: kayan_query;928    time: f32;929    fired: u32;930    hits: u32;931    fires: u32;932    kills: u32;933    breaches: u32;934    came: u32;935}936 937// Kernels: plain loops over plain slices, as in 3.2.938integrate: proc(ps: noalias []position, vs: []const velocity, dt: f32) -> void = {939    for (i: u64 = 0; i < ps.length; i += 1) {940        ps[i].at.x += vs[i].per_second.x * dt;941        ps[i].at.y += vs[i].per_second.y * dt;942    }943}944 945burn: proc(hs: noalias []health, fires: []const burning, dt: f32) -> void = {946    for (i: u64 = 0; i < hs.length; i += 1) {947        hs[i].points -= fires[i].per_second * dt;948    }949}950 951age: proc(ls: noalias []lifetime, dt: f32) -> void = {952    for (i: u64 = 0; i < ls.length; i += 1) {953        ls[i].seconds -= dt;954    }955}956 957bullet_signature: proc() -> u64 = {958    return kayan_mask_of<position>() | kayan_mask_of<velocity>() | kayan_mask_of<damage>() | kayan_mask_of<lifetime>();959}960 961drone_signature: proc() -> u64 = {962    return kayan_mask_of<position>() | kayan_mask_of<velocity>() | kayan_mask_of<health>();963}964 965// Is there a drone in the lane at height y, ahead of x?966drone_ahead: proc(w: *kayan_world, g: *game, x: f32, y: f32) -> b32 = {967    for (i: u64 = 0; i < g[0].drones.tables.length; i += 1) {968        ps: []position = kayan_slice<position>(kayan_query_table(w, g[0].drones&, i));969        for (row: u64 = 0; row < ps.length; row += 1) {970            dy: f32 = ps[row].at.y - y;971            if (dy * dy < 0.25 && ps[row].at.x > x) {972                return true;973            }974        }975    }976    return false;977}978 979// A turret whose timer is up fires, if it has something to fire at.980turret_system: proc(it: *kayan_iter) -> void = {981    g: *game = cast(it[0].ctx, *game);982    ps: []position = kayan_slice<position>(it[0].table);983    ts: []turret = kayan_slice<turret>(it[0].table);984    kayan_query_update(it[0].world, g[0].drones&);985    for (row: u64 = 0; row < ts.length; row += 1) {986        if (ts[row].timer <= 0.0 && drone_ahead(it[0].world, g, ps[row].at.x, ps[row].at.y)) {987            shot: kayan_pending = kayan_defer_spawn(it[0].world, bullet_signature());988            kayan_pending_set<position>(it[0].world, shot, ps[row]);989            kayan_pending_set<velocity>(it[0].world, shot, { .per_second = { .x = 16.0, .y = 0.0 } });990            kayan_pending_set<damage>(it[0].world, shot, { .amount = 25.0 });991            kayan_pending_set<lifetime>(it[0].world, shot, { .seconds = 2.0 });992            ts[row].timer = ts[row].cooldown;993            g[0].fired += 1;994        }995        if (ts[row].timer > 0.0) {996            ts[row].timer -= it[0].dt;997        }998    }999}1000 1001age_system: proc(it: *kayan_iter) -> void = {1002    age(kayan_slice<lifetime>(it[0].table), it[0].dt);1003}1004 1005expire_system: proc(it: *kayan_iter) -> void = {1006    ls: []lifetime = kayan_slice<lifetime>(it[0].table);1007    es: []kayan_entity = kayan_entities(it[0].table);1008    for (row: u64 = 0; row < es.length; row += 1) {1009        if (ls[row].seconds <= 0.0) {1010            kayan_defer_despawn(it[0].world, es[row]);1011        }1012    }1013}1014 1015move_system: proc(it: *kayan_iter) -> void = {1016    integrate(kayan_slice<position>(it[0].table), kayan_slice<velocity>(it[0].table), it[0].dt);1017}1018 1019// A bullet within three quarters of a unit of a drone in its lane hits it. A1020// bullet moves a unit a frame and a drone at most a quarter, so none passes1021// through a drone between two frames without being this close in one of them.1022hit_system: proc(it: *kayan_iter) -> void = {1023    w: *kayan_world = it[0].world;1024    g: *game = cast(it[0].ctx, *game);1025    ps: []position = kayan_slice<position>(it[0].table);1026    ds: []damage = kayan_slice<damage>(it[0].table);1027    es: []kayan_entity = kayan_entities(it[0].table);1028    kayan_query_update(w, g[0].drones&);1029    for (b: u64 = 0; b < es.length; b += 1) {1030        for (i: u64 = 0; i < g[0].drones.tables.length; i += 1) {1031            t: *kayan_table = kayan_query_table(w, g[0].drones&, i);1032            tps: []position = kayan_slice<position>(t);1033            ths: []health = kayan_slice<health>(t);1034            for (row: u64 = 0; row < tps.length; row += 1) {1035                dx: f32 = tps[row].at.x - ps[b].at.x;1036                dy: f32 = tps[row].at.y - ps[b].at.y;1037                if (dx * dx < 0.5625 && dy * dy < 0.25) {1038                    ths[row].points -= ds[b].amount;1039                    kayan_defer_despawn(w, es[b]);1040                    g[0].hits += 1;1041                }1042            }1043        }1044    }1045}1046 1047// Below half health, a drone catches fire: a component added, so a command.1048ignite_system: proc(it: *kayan_iter) -> void = {1049    g: *game = cast(it[0].ctx, *game);1050    hs: []health = kayan_slice<health>(it[0].table);1051    es: []kayan_entity = kayan_entities(it[0].table);1052    for (row: u64 = 0; row < es.length; row += 1) {1053        if (hs[row].points < 0.5 * hs[row].max && hs[row].points > 0.0) {1054            kayan_defer_add<burning>(it[0].world, es[row], { .per_second = 10.0 });1055            g[0].fires += 1;1056        }1057    }1058}1059 1060burn_system: proc(it: *kayan_iter) -> void = {1061    burn(kayan_slice<health>(it[0].table), kayan_slice<burning>(it[0].table), it[0].dt);1062}1063 1064die_system: proc(it: *kayan_iter) -> void = {1065    g: *game = cast(it[0].ctx, *game);1066    hs: []health = kayan_slice<health>(it[0].table);1067    es: []kayan_entity = kayan_entities(it[0].table);1068    for (row: u64 = 0; Advanced · seven lessons

Layout and SIMD

docs/README.md

Seven lessons for after Build an ECS. The course builds the ECS. These go underneath it, to the memory and the machine code:

  • Lesson 1, aos vs soa. The same particles in three layouts: what a loop fetches per cache line, what noalias promises the compiler, which loops it vectorizes, and how to check that in the assembly.
  • Lessons 2 to 6 build an archetype ECS again, compressed into five steps, and end with a small game. They came first and move fast. After the course, read them as a recap, or as a second take on the same design. Lesson 4 builds the world in includes/kayan.rin, and lessons 5 and 6 import it unchanged.
  • Lesson 7, layout follows access. Four layouts under streams and under random lookups, timed, and how an ECS decides where each component lives.
  • Lesson 0, from kayan, reviews the original C kayan: what these lessons kept from it, what they changed, and why.
lessonabout
0from kayanwhat was kept from the C kayan, what changed, and why
1aos vs soathe same particles in three layouts, what a loop fetches, and what SIMD needs
2archetype tableone table: columns, rows, spawn, swap-remove, systems over slices
3many archetypesone table type for every archetype: ids, signatures, queries
4entity handlesgenerational handles, slots, moving between archetypes
5inspectorprinting and editing any entity from reflection records
6kayana small game, and deferring structural changes to a command buffer
7access patternsfour layouts under streams and lookups, and how an ECS decides

How to read them

Read each lesson's .rin file from the top. It opens with the problem it solves, and the code follows in the order it runs. Then run it and read the output against the code: every lesson prints what it does, step by step. The guides here give the background that doesn't fit in a file header, and end with exercises.

Timings only mean something in a Release build. Debug checks every slice index. Lesson 1's guide shows how to build one, and what to look for in the disassembly.

Advanced · lesson 0 · review

From kayan

docs/0_from_kayan.md

kayan is a sketch of an archetype entity component system in C, about 200 lines in src/kayan.h, with haikal generating its containers. These lessons start from its idea and rebuild the rest. This page says what was kept, what was changed, and why, so the lessons can be read as a review of it as much as a rewrite.

What kayan does

Components are bits in an enum, positions = 1 << 0, velocities = 1 << 1 and so on. Each archetype is a C struct written by hand (A, B, C, D) that starts with an ArchetypeHeader and then holds one haikal Array_T per component. The header has a u64 signature and a Map_u64 from column name to the column's byte offset in the struct.

A query walks an array of void * pointing at the archetypes, reads each header, and tests (signature & want) == want. For a match it looks up "positions" and "velocities" in the offset map, adds the offsets to the struct's address, and runs the loop over the two columns.

Kept

  • An archetype is a struct of arrays. Each component is a contiguous column and every entity in the table has every column. That is the whole point, and kayan had it right from the start.
  • A signature is a u64 of component bits, and a query is the test (signature & all) == all. Lesson 3 adds a none mask beside it.
  • Arenas for all of it. Nothing in these lessons is freed one at a time.

Changed

  • One table type for every archetype (lesson 3). kayan needs a new C struct, a new signature line and new offset-map lines for every archetype. Here an archetype is data: a signature, and the world makes its table the first time something needs it (lesson 4).
  • Columns by component id, not by name (lesson 3). kayan hashes the strings "positions" and "velocities" on every query. Here a table's columns are an array indexed by component id, so finding one is an index. Names are kept for tools, through reflection (lesson 5).
  • The signature comes from the columns (lesson 3). In kayan they are written separately and can disagree. In D they do: it has positions and velocities columns, but its signature is health | damage | alive, so the movement query never visits it.
  • A row is added and removed in one place (lesson 2). kayan appends to each column at the call site, and keeps entity_count apart from the columns. For B and D it increments a's count instead of their own (kayan.h lines 142, 145, 168, 174), so A reports seven entities and the others report none. Nothing breaks only because the query loop happens to use the column's own length.
  • Entities have handles (lesson 4). kayan's entity id is the value of an archetype's entity_count before it is bumped: meant per table, in practice A's, as above. Nothing records where an entity lives, so there is no way to refer to one entity from elsewhere, to remove it, or to move it to another archetype. The lessons use an {index, generation} handle and a slot list that tracks each entity's table and row.
  • Entities move between archetypes (lesson 4). Adding or removing a component moves the entity to the matching table, copying the components both tables share.
  • Structural changes wait for the end of the frame (lesson 6), through a command buffer in a frame arena. kayan never changes structure while a query runs, but only because it never changes structure at all.
  • Reflection replaces hand-written tables (lessons 3 to 5). A component's size and alignment come from T<>, and so do the names a tool prints. The offset map goes away entirely.

Not carried over

  • **vec4s for positions.** kayan pads 3D vectors to 16 bytes, which suits SIMD loads. The lessons use vec2 and vec3 and plain loops, and leave vectorizing to the C compiler. noalias on the kernels' parameters, in lessons 1, 2, 3 and 6, lets it do that without run-time overlap checks. Lesson 1 adds a third layout, one f32 array per coordinate, which is the one SIMD runs cleanly over, and its exercises come back to vec4. Lesson 7 weighs that layout against lookups, which it is bad at.
  • cglm and the haikal containers. rin's generics and std (vec<T>, hashmap<K, V>, slices) cover what they did.

Small things in kayan.h

  • The query's inner loop declares i32 i, shadowing the outer i (line 201).
  • Each lookup on lines 199 and 200 hashes and compares a string, once per column per archetype per query. That is cheap next to a large loop, but it is work that an array index does for nothing.

Advanced · lesson 1

AoS vs SoA

src/1.aos_vs_soa/aos_vs_soa.rin

src/1.aos_vs_soa/aos_vs_soa.rin

The same 262,144 particles, stored three times: as an array of 68-byte particle structs (AoS), as seven arrays, one per field (SoA), and with position and velocity split one step further into six arrays of f32, one per coordinate (split). Sixty steps of movement run over each, and the program checks that all three end with the same positions.

What the loop fetches

Memory reaches the CPU in 64-byte cache lines. A loop that reads 24 bytes of each 68-byte particle still pulls every byte of every line those particles sit in, so about two thirds of what movement fetches in the AoS loop is tint, age, lifetime, size and name. In the SoA loop the two arrays it reads are the only thing it fetches, and the hardware prefetcher sees two simple streams. The split loop fetches the same 24 bytes per particle as SoA, as six streams.

The program prints that arithmetic:

bytes fetched per step: 17825792     (AoS: 68 bytes x 262144)
bytes fetched per step: 6291456      (SoA: 24 bytes x 262144)
bytes fetched per step: 6291456      (split: 6 x 4 bytes x 262144)

What the CPU does with each layout

SSE registers hold four floats, AVX registers eight. One instruction adds four (or eight) pairs of floats at once, but only if they arrive side by side. Here is what clang-cl /O2 makes of each loop for Windows x64, read from the object file:

loopparticles per passinstructions per passper particleshuffles
move_aos116161
move_soa477about 1930
move_split42050
move_split, /arch:AVX2814under 20
  • AoS goes one particle at a time: each particle's fields are 68 bytes from the next particle's, so there is nothing to load four of.
  • SoA is vectorized, four particles per pass, but each vec3 keeps x, y and z side by side. To get four x's into one register the compiler loads them one float at a time and stitches them together, then takes them apart again to store. About a tenth of the loop is arithmetic, and per particle it costs about what AoS does.
  • Split is what SIMD wants. Each line of move_split becomes one load of four consecutive floats, one multiply, one add, one store:
  movups (%r11,%rdi,4), %xmm4     four vx
  movups (%rcx,%rdi,4), %xmm5     four px
  mulps  %xmm1, %xmm4             vx * dt
  addps  %xmm5, %xmm4             px + vx * dt
  movups %xmm4, (%rcx,%rdi,4)     four px back

A layout is right for SIMD when its vector loop is mostly full-width loads, math and stores. When it is mostly movss, unpcklps and shufps, the data is fighting the registers.

Split is right for this loop, which runs over every particle in order. It is wrong for a loop that reaches particles by index, where x, y and z in three arrays are three trips to memory instead of one. Lesson 7 measures both kinds of loop over four layouts.

Timings

--time prints how long each layout took. Release builds, best of five runs, on the 2.8 GHz Xeon these lessons were checked on, ms:

buildAoSSoAsplit
clang -O249.626.916.5
clang -O347.526.715.9
clang -O2 -mavx2 -mfma47.918.613.0
gcc -O334.213.714.2
gcc -O246.121.344.3

The same loops with 8,192 particles, so everything stays in L2, and 1,920 steps so the work is the same:

buildAoSSoAsplit
clang -O224.125.611.9
clang -O2 -mavx2 -mfma28.617.86.5
gcc -O312.712.08.9
  • In cache, split is the only layout SIMD helps much. SoA and AoS come out about even in L2 on clang, as the instruction counts say they should.
  • From the 6 MB case, SoA's smaller footprint shows. That machine has 33 MB of L3, so the data stays in cache between steps, but SoA and split still move a third of the bytes AoS does.
  • **gcc -O2 does not vectorize across particles at all,** so split, with six streams and nothing gained for them, is its slowest layout. gcc users want -O3. clang-cl, rin's default, is the clang rows.

The machine is shared; expect about 20 percent noise between runs. Debug numbers are not worth comparing: every positions[i] is bounds checked there.

For a Release build, set build_type to "Release" in build.rin and run rin build again. Release defines NDEBUG, which compiles the bounds checks out. Or compile the C that tools/check.py leaves in build/check/aos_vs_soa/ with -O2 -DNDEBUG.

The parameter list is the data

move_aos(ps: noalias []particle, ...) says it needs particles. move_soa(positions: noalias []vec3, velocities: noalias []vec3, ...) and move_split(px, py, pz, vx, vy, vz, ...) say exactly which data they read and write. In lessons 2 and 3 every system is written that way. In lesson 6 each system runs its own query, then works only on the columns it named.

Naming the columns is what lets a scheduler see that two systems touch different data, and it is what makes a system easy to test: hand it two small arrays.

noalias

As far as the C compiler can tell, two []vec3 slices could overlap. So before it works on several particles at once, it checks at run time that the two are apart, and keeps a one-at-a-time copy of the loop for when they are not. noalias on a parameter promises that, for the call, nothing else reaches the memory behind it. The check and the second copy go away.

The SoA loop without and with it, Release, ms:

buildwithout noaliaswith noalias
gcc -O331.713.4
gcc -O220.521.3
clang -O226.326.5
  • **gcc -O3** is where it shows. Without the promise, its checked vector loop was slower than not vectorizing at all (21 ms with -fno-tree-loop-vectorize), and the SoA loop lost to the AoS one.
  • clang vectorized the loop either way. Its check runs once per call, so removing it saves nothing that shows here.

On Windows, one slice needs it too. move_aos has a single slice, which cannot overlap another, and it still takes noalias. Windows passes a slice to a proc by reference, as a pointer to a copy, and clang-cl does not use C's type rules to decide what can overlap (it matches MSVC). So, without the promise, a float written through ps might be the slice's own pointer or length, and the loop reads both again after every particle:

mov   r8,qword ptr [rcx]                   ps.data, every particle
movss xmm2,dword ptr [gravity]             gravity, every particle
...
cmp   rdx,qword ptr [rcx+8]                ps.length, every particle

With noalias the compiler gets the pointer and the length once, in registers, and the loop is 16 instructions instead of 19.

**And gravity is static.** A global that other files could reach is, to gcc, something a write through a slice might change, even through a noalias one, so gcc -O3 put a run-time check in front of move_split's vector loop. gravity: static f32 keeps it to this file, nothing takes its address, and the check goes away. Passing it as a parameter would do the same.

The promise is checked in Debug. Pass soa.positions as both arguments to move_soa and the Debug build stops before the loop runs:

aos_vs_soa.rin:138: noalias parameters 'positions' and 'velocities' overlap

A Release build does not check. It runs on, and the lesson prints same result: no.

Fused multiply-add

With -mfma, -march=native or clang-cl's /arch:AVX2, clang fuses p + v * dt into one instruction that rounds once instead of twice. All three layouts are fused the same way and still agree, but the checksum's last digits move, from 38572460.505 to 38572460.519, and the byte-for-byte check against aos_vs_soa.expected fails. tools/check.py builds without those flags.

When AoS is right

When the code that touches a record touches most of its fields, AoS fetches nothing wasted, and keeping a record together is simpler. Data-oriented design does not mean SoA everywhere. It means choosing the layout from the loops that run over it. An entity component system is the case where many small loops each touch a few fields.

Try

  1. Run with --time in Release. Then remove tint, age, lifetime and name from particle and run again. The AoS loop should close most of the gap, because the struct shrinks toward what the loop reads.
  2. Add /arch:AVX2 to build_c_flags and compare --time. Then read move_split in the disassembly: eight floats per register, and vfmadd.
  3. kayan stored positions as 16-byte vec4s. Change vec3 to four floats and see what it does to the bytes-per-step line, to move_soa's disassembly and to the timing.
  4. Store the split columns in blocks of eight, { x: [8]f32; y: [8]f32; ... }, and write the loop over blocks. Each block is a whole AVX register per coordinate, and a particle's coordinates stay near each other.
  5. Remove noalias from move_soa and build Release with gcc -O3. Compare --time, then compile with -fopt-info-vec and find "loop versioned for vectorization because of possible aliasing".
  6. Remove static from gravity, build with gcc -O3 -fopt-info-vec, and find the same message for move_split.
  7. Pass soa.positions as both arguments to move_soa. Run it in Debug, then in Release.
